text: I recently opened a checking account with Regions Bank and began using it for direct deposit of my paycheck. During this transition, I experienced a delay in receiving one paycheck due to a payroll processing issue related to a change in direct deposit. As a result, my account balance became negative. Between approximately XX/XX/year>, Regions Bank charged seven overdraft fees of {$72.00} each, totaling {$430.00}, within a very short period of time. These fees were not the result of separate spending events but occurred as a cascade from the same delayed deposit and timing issue. The rapid accumulation of these fees significantly increased my negative balance and made it difficult to recover financially. This created a financial hardship situation. I contacted Regions Bank to request assistance. They refunded one overdraft fee but declined to reverse the remaining fees, despite the fact that all charges stemmed from the same underlying issue. I am requesting that Regions Bank review this situation and provide a reasonable resolution, including reversal of additional overdraft fees associated with this event. I have since taken steps to prevent this from happening again, including changing my banking arrangements and updating my direct deposit. This complaint concerns excessive overdraft fees charged in a short timeframe tied to a single deposit delay event.

text: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint Regarding Capital One Dispute Handling Complainant : XXXX XXXX Account : Capital One Credit Card Disputed Amount : {$2700.00} Transaction Date : XX/XX/XXXX Merchant : XXXX XXXX XXXX I am filing this complaint regarding Capital Ones handling of my billing dispute under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ). DISPUTE FACTS On XX/XX/XXXX, I purchased prepaid services totaling {$2700.00} ( {$2500.00} plus a 3.5 % credit card surcharge ). Approximately 15 hours later, on XX/XX/XXXX, I cancelled all future services. My cancellation was confirmed in writing via email. At the time of purchase, I was not provided with any written refund or cancellation policy. No such policy appeared on my receipt, in the merchants app, or at the point of sale. After cancellation, the merchant confirmed that a refund check would be issued. A check was issued ; however, the merchant later placed a stop payment on that check. I obtained official documentation from XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX confirming the stop payment. The services were never rendered. DISPUTE TIMELINE WITH CAPITAL ONE XX/XX/XXXX Capital One denied the dispute, stating the merchant provided confirmation showing no cancellation per policy. XX/XX/XXXX I contacted Capital One and was instructed to provide additional documentation. XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXX ) I submitted the following documentation : Cancellation confirmation email dated XX/XX/XXXX Text communications confirming cancellation Receipts showing no refund policy disclosure Copy of the issued refund check XXXX XXXX XXXX documentation confirming stop payment on that check Written narrative explanation XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX Capital One denied the dispute again citing insufficient documentation. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX I resubmitted all documentation along with written clarification. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX XXXX Capital One issued a third denial within approximately 12 hours and advised that I resolve the matter directly with the merchant. CONCERN REGARDING REASONABLE INVESTIGATION Under 15 U.S.C. 1666 of the Fair Credit Billing Act, a creditor must conduct a reasonable investigation of a billing dispute before denying a claim. The rapid denial timelines approximately three hours after documentation submission and approximately twelve hours after resubmission raise concern that a meaningful review of the submitted evidence may not have occurred. The denial letters do not specify : What documentation was reviewed Why cancellation confirmation was insufficient Why stop-payment documentation was insufficient What specific information was missing This dispute concerns services not delivered as agreed and failure to disclose material terms at the time of sale.

Request for Federal Investigation and Corrective Action To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint to formally request an investigation into Valley Bank for discriminatory denial of banking services arising from the conduct of a branch manager at a XXXX, New Jersey location. The facts of this case demonstrate a serious civil-rights and fair-banking concern that extends beyond my individual experience and raises risk of systemic harm to other customers. 

Background and Timeline : On XX/XX/XXXX, I visited Valley Banks XXXX XXXX XXXX, located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, NJ XXXX, to open a personal checking account. I provided valid government-issued identification, completed all required XXXX ( XXXX ) and account-opening procedures with a personal banker, and was approved through Valley Banks systems. 
The account was successfully opened, activated with online banking access, and later issued a debit card and official online banking enrollment letter mailed to my address. These actions confirm that Valley Banks compliance, identity verification, and risk controls were fully satisfied. 

Discriminatory Intervention and False Statement : After the account was opened, the branch manager, identified as XXXX, personally intervened and instructed the banker to close the account. I was told by the manager that the account was never opened, a statement that is demonstrably false based on Valley Banks own documentation, system access, and debit card issuance. 
No fraud, sanctions, identity issue, documentation deficiency, or compliance-based reason was provided for this closure. The termination occurred solely after the managers discretionary intervention. 

Ongoing Harm and Confirmation of Irregularity : When I later attempted to open an account at another Valley Bank branch located at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, NJ XXXX, I was denied service solely because the account had been opened and closed on the same day. The second branch manager stated that such a same-day open-and-close sequence is not normal and required explanation from the original branch. 
As a result of the initial managers actions, I was effectively barred from banking services at Valley Bank without justification. 

Basis for Discrimination Concern : Based on the successful completion of all compliance requirements, the manual override by a branch manager after observing me in person, the lack of any legitimate banking or compliance reason, the false statement that the account did not exist, and the ongoing denial of service across branches, I believe this conduct constitutes discriminatory denial of the right to make and enforce a financial contract in violation of 42 U.S.C. 1981, applicable fair-banking laws, and federal consumer protection standards. 

Broader Public Interest : I am filing this complaint not only to seek accountability for my own experience, but to prevent similar conduct from occurring to other customers, particularly immigrants and people of color, who may not have the resources or documentation to challenge such treatment.

These points are linked to my American Express XXXX XXXX card, which provides premium redemption benefits including a 35 % Pay With Points rebate on my selected airline ( XXXX XXXX ) when booking through Amex XXXX, promotional transfer bonuses to airline and hotel partners, and full access to the Amex XXXX redemption platform. I called Amex on XX/XX/XXXX XXXX days after Amex internally identified the system migration issue and was told to wait XXXX hours. No one mentioned a systemic issue. We jointly agreed to create a second XXXX XXXX and port the XXXX point balance from the old account to the new one as a workaround. At no point during this call was I told that the underlying cause was a known system migration affecting multiple customers. Had I known this, I would not have agreed to create a new account structure on top of an already-unstable platform migration. I would have waited for the engineering fix. The new account could not receive the transfer. I was told to wait XXXX hours. XX/XX/XXXX XXXX MORE CALLS, THREE MORE MISDIRECTIONS - Call XXXX ( XX/XX/XXXX, evening ) : Follow-up. No resolution. - Call XXXX ( XX/XX/XXXX minutes ) : A different representative identified the blocker as a restriction on my Business Checking account. I was transferred to the Checking team, walked through an online verification popup, and the restriction was cleared. The points remained stuck. Still no mention of a systemic issue. - Call XXXX ( XX/XX/XXXX minutes ) : I was told a back-end team needed to close an open ticket. Target date : XX/XX/XXXX. I was told to wait. XX/XX/XXXX PROMISED DATE PASSES WITH NO COMMUNICATION XX/XX/XXXX came and went. No callback. No resolution. No email. No notification. I waited XXXX additional days. XX/XX/XXXX SUPERVISOR CALL MAKES THINGS ACTIVELY WORSE On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again and was escalated to a supervisor who identified herself as " XXXX '' ( spelled C-E-R-A ) from the Banking Servicing XXXX department XXXX The call lasted XXXX hour and XXXX minutes. Critical event during the call : When the call began, I could still see my full XXXX point balance in my credit card redemption interface. During the call, an Amex back-end process re-linked my Business Checking account from my original XXXX XXXX ( XXXX points ) to the secondary XXXX XXXX ( XXXX points ). As a result, the XXXX balance disappeared from my credit card redemption interface in real time during the supervisor call. I have screenshots taken at XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX showing both XXXX XXXX visible ( XXXX and XXXX ) proving the full balance was accessible before the mid-call change. The supervisor verbally acknowledged during the call : XXXX. The XXXX points still exist in Amex 's system. 2. I have done nothing as a customer to cause these points to become ineligible or unusable. 3. The current state is a result of Amex 's own back-end changes. 4. The workaround ( second XXXX XXXX ) created " a multi-department situation that should not have been a multi-department situation. '' XXXX. Her intention was to " refresh these points availability. '' She committed to a callback within XXXX business days. She declined to provide a ticket number, employee ID, or written confirmation. XX/XX/XXXX THE INSTITUTIONAL ISSUE IS FINALLY DISCLOSED On XX/XX/XXXX, supervisor XXXX called back ( XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX minutes ). For the first time in XXXX calls over 22 days, she disclosed : XXXX. The issue is institutional related to a system migration to a central Amex platform. XXXX. It affects multiple customers, not just my account. XXXX. Amex has known about it since approximately XX/XX/XXXX. 4. There is no ETA for resolution. She stated it will not be resolved within the next 30 days. Her proposed interim solution was for me to redeem the points as cash through the checking account. I declined. I accumulated these points over years specifically for travel, not cash. Cashing out would force me to accept approximately {$7500.00} in cash value for points worth over {$18000.00} in travel value through my XXXX XXXX card 's benefits a 58 % loss. When I asked for a Customer Relations referral, she said she did not have XXXX. She provided an automated complaint line ( XXXX ). THE FINANCIAL HARM Points value trapped in degraded profile : The XXXX points are currently accessible only through my checking account XXXX XXXX, which offers basic cash redemption and XXXX partner transfers with no promotional bonuses. My Business Platinum card 's XXXX XXXX which I pay an annual fee for include : - 35 % Pay With Points airline rebate : I have selected XXXX XXXX. The full XXXX cap of XXXX points is unused. This benefit alone is worth XXXX points ( {$3500.00} {$5300.00} ) that I can not access because the points are in the wrong XXXX XXXX. - XXXX transfer bonuses of 2040 % to airline and hotel partners ( credit card XXXX XXXX, not available through checking ). - Amex XXXX booking access with XXXX pricing. Travel plans in jeopardy : I have a XXXX trip planned for XXXX XXXX that I intended to fund using these XXXX points. These points were not accumulated casually they represent years of deliberate saving toward high-value travel redemption. I am now facing the real possibility of having to cancel this trip entirely, because paying cash for flights and hotels that I planned to cover with XXXX XXXX is not financially viable. Constructive forfeiture : I want to be clear about what " the points still exist '' actually means in practice. But points that can only be redeemed at basic cash value stripped of the 35 % airline rebate, promotional transfer bonuses, and Amex XXXX access that I pay a XXXX XXXX annual fee for are not the same points I accumulated. Telling a customer " your points are safe '' while removing the redemption benefits that make them worth accumulating is a constructive forfeiture of value, even if the nominal balance is unchanged. Time investment : XXXX calls totaling approximately XXXX hours XXXX minutes across 22 days. WHAT AMERICAN EXPRESS HAS FAILED TO DO XXXX. Disclose a known issue. Amex knew about the system migration since XX/XX/XXXX. I was not told until XX/XX/XXXX after XXXX calls and a workaround that made things worse. 2. Issue a ticket or case number. Across seven calls including a supervisor escalation, no ticket number has ever been provided. 3. Provide any written confirmation. Every commitment has been verbal only. 4. A mid-call back-end change on XX/XX/XXXX made the points less accessible, not more. 6. Offer an adequate resolution. Description of What Happened Company : Ava ( Ava Finance , Inc. ) Issue : Fee-Harvester Violation ( 12 CFR 1026.52 ( a ) ) & Unfair/Abusive Billing ( Account Lockout ) I am filing this complaint because Ava is violating the 25 % fee-harvester cap under 12 CFR 1026.52 ( a ) and engaging in unfair billing practices by charging fees for an account I can not access. 1. Federal Fee Cap Violation : Ava reports this account to credit bureaus as a 'Credit Card ' with a {$270.00} limit. Under federal law, total non-penalty fees in the first year can not exceed {$67.00} ( 25 % of {$270.00} ). The Math : Ava reports a credit limit of {$270.00} to the bureaus but charges a mandatory monthly fee of {$9.00}. This totals {$110.00} per yearwhich is 43 % of the credit limit. This far exceeds the federal 25 % cap ( {$67.00} ) for first-year accounts. The company 's attempt to rebrand this as a 'membership ' is a deceptive workaround, as the fee is required to maintain the credit line. 2. Account Lockout & Abusive Billing : I am currently locked out of my account and have no access to the credit line or my account management tools. Despite this complete lack of service, Ava continues to withdraw {$9.00} monthly from my bank account. Charging fees for a withheld service is an Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Act ( UDAAP ). 3. Attempted Resolution : I have attempted to regain access and dispute these fees, but the company has not provided a resolution. I am a student and a manager in the food service industry ; I do not have the time or resources to act as a compliance officer for a company that ignores federal lending laws. Also, Ava will claim the {$9.00} is a " membership fee. '' However, : " The fee is a mandatory condition of the credit line. If I stop paying the 'membership, ' they close the 'credit card. ' Therefore, under Regulation Z, this is a finance charge/fee related to the issuance of credit and must be capped at 25 %. Also the fee was applied in the first place to even access the card. Ava is reporting an 'Open-End Credit Card ' to TransUnion/Experian. They can not claim to be a 'utility/membership ' service while simultaneously reporting to the bureaus as a 'revolving credit line. ' They are misrepresenting the nature of their product to bypass consumer protections. I have been denied access to my account for [ 9+ MONTHS!!! ] while monthly drafts continue. On XX/XX/year> I purchased an item on XXXX ( Item # XXXX ) for {$690.00} using PayPal Credit, which is issued by Synchrony Bank. Shortly after the purchase, XXXX removed the original listing due to suspicious activity, indicating the transaction was likely fraudulent. Despite this, the seller later uploaded a XXXX tracking number showing Delivered. However, this tracking number was part of a known zip code tracking scam, where a seller sends a package to a random address within the buyers ZIP code to generate a Delivered scan that can defeat automated fraud systems. The package was never delivered to my home address associated with the order. I confirmed this with my local XXXX post office. The postmaster verified that the tracking number associated with my order was delivered to a different address, not to my residence. I also filed reports with XXXX for mail fraud and with the FBIs Internet Crime Complaint Center ( IC3 ). I opened a billing dispute with Synchrony Bank ( PayPal Credit ) for merchandise not received. However, Synchrony closed the dispute after contacting XXXX and relying solely on the sellers tracking number showing Delivered. Synchrony did not appear to review the underlying fraud indicators, the removal of the listing for suspicious activity, or the confirmation from XXXX that the package was not delivered to my address. By relying only on a delivery scan without verifying the delivery location or reviewing evidence of fraud, Synchrony failed to conduct a reasonable investigation into my billing dispute. I am requesting that Synchrony Bank : Reopen and properly investigate the dispute for merchandise not received. XXXX the XXXX confirmation that the tracking number was delivered to a different address. Issue a refund of {$690.00} to my PayPal Credit account if the investigation confirms the item was not delivered to me. Consumers should not be held responsible for fraudulent tracking schemes that only show delivery within a ZIP code but not to the actual delivery address. Failure to Conduct a Reasonable Investigation Under the billing dispute protections of the Fair Credit Billing Act, creditors are required to conduct a reasonable investigation when a consumer disputes a charge for merchandise that was not received. In this case, Synchrony Bank appears to have relied solely on a generic delivered tracking status provided by the merchant without verifying whether the package was delivered to my address or reviewing evidence that the tracking number corresponds to a different delivery location. Because the item was never delivered to me and the tracking number has been confirmed by my local XXXX post office as associated with a different address, I believe Synchrony Bank did not conduct a reasonable investigation as required by federal law. He did not disclose that the transaction would be placed into a deferredinterest promotion, that there was a special terms expiration date, or that failing to pay the balance in full by a specific date would result in retroactive interest. If these terms had been explained, I would not have agreed to the financing. I relied on the information provided at the time of purchase, and the required disclosures were not made. When I later contacted Wells Fargo about the unexpected interest charge, they showed me a copy of the disclosure. The disclosure was located on page two, in very small print, and was not something I was shown or made aware of at the time of purchase. I also do not recall ever signing up for paperless statements, and I believe my account may have been switched to paperless without my consent. As a result, I did not receive any mailed disclosures or reminders about the promotional terms or expiration date. About 12 months after the purchase, I enrolled the account in autopay to ensure payments were always made on time. Throughout XXXX and XXXX, I consistently paid above the minimum payment, believing I was paying down a normal balance. I had almost paid the account off in full. Then XX/XX/XXXX, over {$3500.00} in deferred interest was added to my account without warning. This was the first time I became aware that the purchase had been placed in a deferredinterest promotion. The charge was extremely unexpected and financially damaging. I contacted Wells Fargo multiple times to request information and clarification. After receiving the denial, I contacted Wells Fargo again on XX/XX/XXXX to clarify the core issues and was told I would receive a response within 10 business days from XX/XX/XXXX. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX # XXXX XXXX, FL XXXX DOB : XX/XX/XXXX Date : XX/XX/XXXX To Whom It May Concern, This letter serves as a formal demand for immediate deletion of any account currently appearing on my consumer credit report that can not be fully verified with original source documentation, as required by federal law. 
Pursuant to the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1681 ), consumer reporting agencies and furnishers may not report information unless it is complete, accurate, and capable of verification. Verification must be supported by competent evidence, including but not limited to the original signed contract, full account history, and proof of legal authority to report. 
Any account that can not be verified with original source documentationas opposed to automated, summary, or database verificationmust be deleted immediately. Continued reporting of such information constitutes willful noncompliance and failure to maintain maximum possible accuracy.

Additionally, under 15 U.S.C. 1692, any party asserting a debt without lawful validation and proof of standing is prohibited from continued reporting or collection activity.

Further, under the Uniform Commercial Code, including UCC 1-103 and 1-308, the burden of proof rests with the party asserting a financial claim. Absent proof, no enforceable claim exists. 
Accordingly, I hereby demand that you : 1. Immediately delete any account that can not be verified with original source documentation 2. Cease reporting any disputed account lacking such verification 3. Provide written confirmation of deletion 4. Refrain from re-reporting any deleted account without lawful documentation If you contend that any account has been verified, you must provide : The original signed agreement bearing my signature Complete payment and transaction history Proof of ownership and authority to report The method of verification used Failure to comply will result in formal complaints filed with the CFPB, FTC, and State Attorney General, and may subject you to civil liability under 15 U.S.C. 616 and 617.

All rights are expressly reserved without prejudice pursuant to UCC 1-308. 
Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

I am filing this complaint regarding XXXX XXXX  and Portfolio Recovery Associates, LLCfor inaccurate, inconsistent, and misleading credit reporting related to account number Portfolio XXXX, in violation of the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ). 
Proof of Inconsistent and Inaccurate Reporting This same account is being reported differently across the consumer reporting agencies : XXXX  : Reported as a collection XXXX  : Reported as a collection XXXX  : Reported as a charge-off A single account can not legally be reported simultaneously as a collection and a charge-off for the same debt. This conflicting reporting demonstrates that at least one furnisher is reporting inaccurate information. Furnishing inconsistent account statuses violates 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( A ) and 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ), which require information provided to consumer reporting agencies to be accurate, complete, and consistent.

Failure to Issue Required Form 1099-C Despite the account being reported as a charge-offwith XXXX, I have never received a Form 1099-C ( Cancellation of Debt ) from XXXX XXXX  or Portfolio Recovery Associates . If the debt has been charged off and collection activity has ceased or the debt has been abandoned, IRS regulations require the issuance of Form 1099-C reflecting the canceled debt.

Reporting a charge-off while failing to issue a required 1099-C, yet continuing to report or collect the debt elsewhere, is deceptive and misleading and causes financial harm. 
Violations and Harm The actions of XXXX XXXX  and Portfolio Recovery Associates indicate violations of : 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) Furnishing inaccurate information 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( b ) Failure to conduct a reasonable investigation 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) Failure to ensure maximum possible accuracy This inaccurate reporting has damaged my credit profile, caused confusion, and interfered with my ability to obtain credit on fair terms.I am requesting that the CFPB require XXXX XXXX and Portfolio Recovery Associates, LLCto : Correct or delete the inaccurate and inconsistent reporting across allconsumer reporting agencies so the account is reported accurately and uniformly, or removed entirely if it can not be verified.

text: Complaint Against Goldman Sachs regarding Apple Apple Card Fraud Dispute Handling To the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, I am submitting this complaint regarding the handling of an unauthorized transaction dispute on my Apple Card account, issued by Goldman Sachs Bank USA. On XX/XX/year>, my Apple Card account was charged {$52.00} by the merchant XXXX for a transaction I did not authorize, initiate, or benefit from. Upon identifying the unauthorized charge, I promptly contacted Apple Card support and initiated a fraud dispute. Since reporting the fraudulent transaction, I have filed multiple dispute claims under the following case numbers : * XXXX * XXXX * XXXX Despite making these reports in good faith and clearly stating that the transaction was unauthorized, my dispute has now been denied three separate times. My concerns are as follows : 1. I have not been provided with sufficient evidence demonstrating that I authorized this transaction. 2. I have not received a meaningful explanation for why my dispute was denied. 3. I have not been provided transparency regarding the investigative methods used to evaluate my claim. 4. I am concerned that my dispute may not have been investigated thoroughly or in compliance with consumer protection requirements under the Fair Credit Billing Act. As a consumer, I understand that unauthorized credit card transactions are subject to specific protections under federal law, including the right to a fair investigation and a clear explanation of findings. In this case, I believe the dispute resolution process has lacked transparency, fairness, and adequate justification. I am requesting CFPB assistance in obtaining : A full and independent reinvestigation of the disputed transaction. Written documentation of the evidence used to deny my prior claims. A detailed explanation of Goldman Sachs investigative process and findings. Confirmation that my rights under applicable consumer protection laws have been fully honored. Reversal of the unauthorized charge if the investigation confirms that the transaction was fraudulent. Due to the repeated denials and the lack of transparency in resolving this matter, I am escalating this complaint to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau for external review and accountability. Additionally, as a result of the loss of trust in the institutions fraud protection and dispute resolution process, I intend to close my Apple Card account once this matter is resolved. I am requesting that all further communication regarding this matter be provided in writing for documentation purposes. Thank you for your review and assistance.

text:
This complaint supplements CFPB complaint ID XXXX, submitted on XX/XX/XXXX. While that complaint remains under review, Synchrony Bank reissued my Verizon Visa account under a new credit card number, despite the account having been placed on hold and the prior card not set to expire until XX/XX/XXXX. This administrative change has allowed continued fee and interest accrual tied to a canceled Verizon service. 

I opened a Verizon Visa credit card issued by Synchrony Bank more than three years ago as part of a Verizon signup that promoted autopay and paperless billing with bill credits. The card was intended solely to pay Verizon services and was not used for discretionary consumer purchases. 

Over time, our Verizon family plan changed in cost and structure. After paying off phones, all members on the plan disassembled and switched carriers, leaving only my father-in-laws Verizon internet service. I was originally the Verizon account holder, but after the plan changes I lost access to account information and despite extensive calls with Verizon representatives and technical support, access issues were never resolved. 

My father-in-law later switched internet providers but did not immediately cancel Verizon service. As an elderly XXXX veteran living alone, he was unaware of the continued billing. As a result, Verizon service charges accumulated without my knowledge or visibility. Once discovered, my wife and I assisted him in canceling the Verizon internet service, received confirmation of cancellation, and I paid the final Verizon service balance in full, including service-related late charges.

Despite service cancellation and full payment of Verizon charges, late fees and interest continued to accrue on the Synchrony credit card. These penalties were caused by billing design issues, including misalignment between Verizon autopay timing and Synchrony credit card due dates, even when there were no active services and no new purchases. 

At present, the balance on the account consists entirely of late fees and penalty interest, not goods, services, or consumer spending. 

While CFPB complaint ID XXXX is still pending, Synchrony reissued the account under a new card number. This occurred even though the account had been placed on hold and the prior card was not near expiration. I was not requesting a replacement card and did not authorize continued account activity. 

When I contacted Synchrony, multiple representatives stated they could not remove the charges and claimed the account was 7 days in default. However, my records and Synchronys automated phone system stated that the payment due date was XX/XX/XXXX, with a balance of {$46.00}. This discrepancy suggests inaccurate delinquency designation and continued administrative transparency and errors. 

Synchrony representatives confirmed the last account activity was XX/XX/XXXX, with my last payment made XX/XX/XXXX for the full balance at that time. Subsequent late fees and interest were added despite the absence of new charges. Synchrony has refused further adjustments solely because a courtesy reversal occurred within the prior 12 months, even though this matter involves a closed underlying service and fee-only balance caused by billing structure and account administration. 

Additionally, Synchronys automated phone system makes it extremely difficult to reach a representative, repeatedly routing calls through promotional offers and unrelated services before allowing access to account assistance. 

This situation has caused unnecessary financial harm and ongoing stress. I have made repeated good-faith efforts to resolve this directly with Synchrony, but internal policy limitations have prevented resolution despite the absence of any legitimate underlying charges.

text:
I am filing this complaint against Synchrony Bank regarding an unresolved billing error on my PayPal Credit account. 

On XX/XX/year>, I used PayPal Credit ( issued by Synchrony Bank ) to purchase a XXXX XXXX XXXX rowing machine for {$440.00}. The product arrived defective and never functioned as intended. 

I contacted the merchant within the return period and repeatedly thereafter. The merchant acknowledged in writing that the equipment arrived broken and attempted to cure the defect by sending replacement parts, but the product was never repaired or made usable. The merchant ultimately refused to issue a refund. 

I disputed the charge through PayPal/Synchrony . A provisional credit was issued, but on XX/XX/year>, that provisional credit was reversed, and the {$440.00} balance was re-posted to my PayPal Credit account. As a result, I remain financially liable for the charge and was required to pay it to avoid interest and credit harm. 

I made that payment under protest solely to avoid finance charges and negative credit reporting. 

The merchant has admitted the defect in writing but claims that PayPal overrode the refund and that they no longer owe anything. Synchrony Bank, in turn, has told me to resolve the issue with the merchant and closed the dispute. 

This response is inconsistent with the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) and Regulation Z. The charge represents a billing error because the goods were defective upon delivery, the merchant failed to cure the defect, and no completed refund occurred. A provisional credit that is later reversed does not constitute resolution of a billing error. 

Synchrony Bank has failed to properly investigate and correct this billing error and has improperly shifted merchant risk to the consumer.

text:
Company : Capital One Billing dispute ( a ) no response received from Capital One regarding multiple requests to change dispute category, and ( b ) improperly denied for unspecified information not provided, even though specified information was provided. 


Issue description : I timely filed a dispute for a credit card charge that should have been categorized as Service Not Provided. I mistakenly selected Refund when initiating the dispute. 

I promptly notified Capital One of the error and repeatedly requested that the dispute be reclassified to Service Not Provided. Despite multiple written messages, Capital One has not addressed the reclassification request. Instead, they have sent me XXXX identical requests for documentation that they previously requested when I initially filed as Refund. I have supplied Capital One with all of the documents available to me. My dispute is Service Not Provided the merchant hasnt provided me with Refund documents. Also, the merchant has not delivered the contracted work. This isnt a Refund dispute. 

I have clearly and repeatedly explained that refund-related documentation does not apply. Capital One has failed to take action to reclassify, or even to respond specifically to my reclassification requests. Instead, Capital One continues to send repetitive, seemingly automated requests for the same inapplicable information ( merchants agreement to cancellation/return, that would result in a refund ). 

As a result, I am unable to have my dispute reviewed on the merits due to a procedural error that Capital One refuses to correct. I believe this is a failure of dispute handling and customer service processes. 

In my understanding, under Regulation Z, 12 C.F.R. 1026.13, a billing error includes services not delivered as agreed ( 1026.13 ( a ) ( 3 ) ). The regulation requires only that the consumer provide written notice of a billing error within 60 days of the statement showing the charge ( 1026.13 ( b ) ). Once timely notice is provided, the creditors investigation and resolution obligations run from the original notice date, not from any subsequent reclassification ( 1026.13 ( c ) ). 

Regulation Z does not recognize reclassification as a new dispute ; it requires only timely notice of a billing error for a specific charge, and subsequent clarification does not restart or invalidate that notice. 

Regulation Z contains no provision permitting a creditor to : Deny a timely dispute based on internal dispute coding or chargeback reason codes, Treat a clarification of dispute basis as a new dispute, or Restart or invalidate the XXXX-day notice period due to reclassification. 

Once a creditor receives timely notice of a billing error for a specific charge, the creditors obligations under 1026.13 ( c ) are triggered and run from the original notice date, regardless of later clarification. 

Denying a billing-error dispute because it was initially coded under an incorrect category improperly elevates internal chargeback procedures over federal consumer-protection law and is not supported by Regulation Z.

text:
I am filing this complaint regarding misleading promotional disclosures and undisclosed conditions tied to a Citi credit card balance transfer offer. 

I previously filed a CFPB complaint related to improper payment allocation. That complaint was closed after Citi responded. However, Citis written response introduced a previously undisclosed condition that materially alters how the promotional XXXX operates. This complaint addresses that disclosure issue. 

Citi promoted a balance transfer as 0 % XXXX until XX/XX/year>, after which the XXXX increased to approximately 20.24 % ( annual XXXX ). Based on this disclosure, a reasonable consumer would believe that making payment by the promotional end dateor immediately afterwould avoid interest at the higher rate. 

In Citis written response to CFPB and to the XXXX XXXX Attorney General, Citi stated : In order for the payment to be applied to the expiring balance transfer, the account must cycle before the promotional interest rate is updated to the purchase rate. 

This account cycle requirement was never disclosed in the promotional offer, cardmember agreement, or any balance transfer terms provided to me. 

More importantly, Citis explanation creates a practical impossibility for the consumer to avoid interest : 1. If I made a payment before XX/XX/year>, Citis own payment allocation rules would require that payment to be applied to a different promotional balance with a lower APR ( 0.99 % ), not to the expiring balance transfer. This would not protect me from post-expiration interest. 
2. If I made the payment on or after XX/XX/year>, the date the XXXX increased, Citi claims the payment could not be properly applied unless the account had already cycledan undisclosed internal processing requirement. 

As a result, there was no disclosed or reasonable way for me to comply with the promotion as advertised and avoid interest. The promotional statement of 0 % APR until XX/XX/year> is therefore misleading, because interest liability is actually determined by an undisclosed statement cycle, not the advertised date. 

An undisclosed timing condition that determines whether interest is charged is a material term and must be clearly disclosed. Citis reliance on internal processing rules to deny the consumer the benefit of the advertised promotional APR constitutes misrepresentation by omission. 

Because this logic would apply to any consumer with multiple promotional balances, this appears to be a systemic disclosure issue affecting Citis balance transfer promotions. 

I respectfully request CFPB review of whether Citis promotional disclosures and practices comply with federal consumer protection and Truth in Lending requirements.

I am submitting this follow-up complaint regarding American Expresss continued improper handling of a fraud dispute initially reported in XX/XX/XXXX, and to supplement my prior CFPB complaint reference number XXXX. 

This complaint concerns American Expresss failure to conduct a fair, reasonable, and consumer-protective investigation, as well as abusive, unprofessional, and potentially discriminatory conduct that culminated in a unilateral case resolution issued on XX/XX/XXXX, without further consumer engagement or substantiation. 

In XX/XX/XXXX, I reported unauthorized charges originating from XXXX. A separate financial institution independently investigated the same charges and determined them to be fraudulent. Despite this corroboration, American Express handled the dispute in an adversarial and irregular manner that treated me as a suspect rather than a fraud victim. 

On or about XX/XX/XXXX, I received a voicemail from American Express ( XXXX ) left by an individual identifying himself as XXXX, which disclosed the existence of a fraud investigation and referenced a claim number ( XXXX ) without confirming the identity of the recipient. Initial outreach was improperly made to my work phone number, rather than the contact number associated with my American Express account ( call originating from XXXX ). 

When I returned the call, American Express failed to perform adequate identity authentication prior to discussing sensitive account-specific fraud details. Despite this failure, the representative disclosed confidential information and proceeded to interrogate me in an accusatory and hostile manner. During this interaction, the representative expressly stated I dont believe you and indicated he would be looking for ways to deny the claim, after which he terminated the call. 

Upon calling back, I was told to get lost. Shortly thereafter, I received notice that American Express had issued a final resolution on XX/XX/XXXX, without requesting or accepting any additional informationdespite previously advising that further outreach would occur before a decision was made. 

At no point did American Express provide me with : Any documentation supporting its conclusions Any explanation of what evidence was relied upon Any confirmation that XXXX was contacted to verify the disputed charges Instead, the decision appears to have been based on fabricated or undisclosed information, with no opportunity for rebuttal or clarification. This lack of transparency, combined with hostile verbal conduct and premature resolution, raises serious concerns regarding unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ( UDAAP ). 

Additionally, the tone, disbelief, and dismissive treatment I receivedparticularly statements expressly challenging my credibility without evidenceraise concerns that the decision-making process may have been influenced by improper bias or discriminatory assumptions rather than objective facts.

The representative also instructed me to transmit confidential financial records from another bank via unsecured email, rather than through a secure submission channel. This request, when viewed alongside improper disclosures and hostile conduct, reflects a disregard for consumer data protection and confidentiality obligations. 

I have been an American Express cardholder for over XXXX  years and have never experienced conduct of this nature. The manner in which this matter was handled appears retaliatory, intimidating, and designed to discourage a consumer from exercising their right to report fraud in good faith.

My account was frozen XX/XX/XXXX. Navy Federal sent notice same day as freeze via regular mail only. A {$100.00} service fee was charged XX/XX/XXXX. Under Virginia Code Section 8.01-478 the XXXX expired 90 days after issuance on approximately XX/XX/XXXX. Navy Federal continues to hold my funds approximately 3 months past the legal expiration date with absolutely no legal authority. Continuing to hold funds past XXXX expiration violates Virginia Code Section 8.01-478 and constitutes unlawful retention of funds. My correct address is XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX VA XXXX. I was never properly served with the Writ in violation of Virginia Code Section 8.01-501. Navy Federal accepted and acted on a Writ containing incorrect identifying information. VIOLATION 3 - NO CONFIRMED NOTICE Electronic F und Transfer Act 15 U.S.C. Section 1693 Regulation E 12 C.F.R. Section 1005 Navy Federal sent notice via regular mail only on XX/XX/XXXX the exact same day my account was frozen. Notice was never sent via certified mail with proof of delivery. I never received this notice. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act 15 U.S.C. Section 1693 and Regulation E 12 C.F.R. Section 1005 financial institutions are required to provide adequate notice of account restrictions. Sending notice via regular mail same day as freeze does not constitute adequate notice. VIOLATION 4 - SERVICE FEE CHARGED WITHOUT CONFIRMED NOTICE Electronic Fund Transfer Act 15 U.S.C. Section 1693f On XX/XX/XXXX Navy Federal charged a {$100.00} service fee only 2 days after freezing my account. Notice was sent via regular mail same day as freeze. Regular mail takes 3-5 business days minimum. The fee was charged before I could have possibly received any notice. Under 15 U.S.C. Section 1693f charging fees without proper notice violates my rights under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act. VIOLATION 5 - ONLINE ACCESS COMPLETELY REMOVED Electronic Fund Transfer Act 15 U.S.C. Section 1693b Regulation E 12 C.F.R. Section 1005 Navy Federal completely removed my online account access on XX/XX/XXXX. Under 15 U.S.C. Section 1693b and Regulation E 12 C.F.R. Section 1005 financial institutions can not restrict account access beyond what is legally authorized. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX does not authorize complete removal of online account access. I have had absolutely no online access for over 4 months with no legal basis. VIOLATION XXXX - REFUSED PHONE COMMUNICATION Virginia Consumer Protection Act Section 59.1-196 Navy Federal refused all phone communication regarding this matter for the past month forcing me to visit a branch in person as the only means of resolution. Under Virginia Consumer Protection Act Section 59.1-196 this constitutes an unfair and deceptive business practice creating deliberate barriers to resolution. VIOLATION 7 - VOICE RECORDING REQUIREMENT Virginia Consumer Protection Act Section 59.1-196 Consumer Financial Protection Act 12 U.S.C. Section 5531 Navy Federal required a voice recording as a condition of receiving phone assistance. When I refused I was told I must visit a branch. Under Virginia Consumer Protection Act Section 59.1-196 and Consumer Financial Protection Act 12 U.S.C. Section 5531 this constitutes an unfair abusive and deceptive practice used as leverage to deny me assistance. VIOLATION 8 - HOLDING FUNDS PAST WRIT EXPIRATION Virginia Code Section 8.01-478 As of XX/XX/XXXX Navy Federal continues to hold my funds approximately 3 months past the XX/XX/XXXX expiration of the Writ. Under Virginia Code Section 8.01-478 Navy Federal has no legal authority to continue holding these funds past expiration. This constitutes unlawful conversion of my funds. VIOLATION 9 - INVALID UNDERLYING JUDGMENT Virginia Code Section 8.01-296 Virginia Code Section 8.01-322 The underlying judgment from XX/XX/XXXX was obtained without proper service in violation of Virginia Code Sections 8.01-296 and 8.01-322. On XX/XX/XXXX, I made a large deposit of {$1000.00}. I know it had XXXX {$100.00} bills, and the rest was a mix of {$20.00}, {$10.00}, {$5.00} and mainly {$1.00} bills. Due to the large number of singles, the stack was too big to deposit at once, so I split it up into 2 deposits. The first stack had all the {$100.00}, {$20.00}, {$10.00}, {$5.00} and maybe some {$1.00} bills. A {$5.00} bill had a bent corner, so it got spit back out and I'm fairly certain the screen reflected that {$960.00} was deposited at this point. So, I straightened that bill out and added it to my stack of singles I had left and went to deposit it. At first, the deposit thing went to close on top of the stack, and I didn't have them positioned good, so I took the money out because I didnt want it to cause an issue. I then hit deposit more and this time successfully put the stack in the machine. At this point, I hear the ATM sound like it's processing my second deposit. It spits out a {$1.00} bill that was bent and then tells me thank you for banking at Chase and closed me out. I didn't get a screen where it showed me my total deposit or if I wanted to print a receipt, just ended the transaction abruptly. Since there were other people behind me, I didn't want to take longer than needed so I drove around to park and checked my bank account to see if it all processed correctly. I saw my bank account only reflected the {$960.00} deposit and not the full {$1000.00}. I went inside the branch, and I explained what happened to an employee and they told me that I had to call the number on the back of my debit card. The second I got home ; I made that call and filed a claim and explained everything that happened to the claims department. They gave me temporary credit for the missing {$56.00} on XX/XX/XXXX while they did their research. Then 4 days later on XX/XX/XXXX, I got a new letter that stated they researched the transaction I reported and found that the transaction was processed according to the information you provided or was authorized, that as a result they were removing the {$56.00} from my account on XX/XX/XXXX and to contact them if I would like to request the information they used for their research. I called them again right after reading that and asked them to explain what happened because the letter made no sense. They stated that after their research, nothing supported what I said, so they were taking the {$56.00} back and the claim was closed. They kept asking if I was sure and basically doubting what I said was accurate, so I asked to speak to a supervisor. The supervisor explained that they audited the machine and showed no overage, but he did see there was an error message of some type, so he was reopening the claim for that to get further investigated. He said I would hear back in 3-5 days, so on day 5, XX/XX/XXXX, I called back and was told it was still being investigated, and it would really take 10 days. On XX/XX/XXXX I called back for an update where they said after further investigation, that the deposit was processed correctly for {$960.00} and the claim is now closed. I asked what steps were taken to determine this and kept being told that the backend team had those details not the claims department. I said I got a letter stating I could contact them if I would like to request the information they used for their research so thats what I was doing. I just kept getting told they dont have that information and that the backend team doesnt have a phone number so I couldnt speak with them. I asked if they could give me information on my deposit such as how many of each bill denomination was deposited, if they could see 2 deposits were made in the one transaction or if the cameras of the ATM were checked to see if the ATM spit out extra money when it shouldnt have. She told me once again that the claims department doesnt have any of that information. I then asked to speak to a supervisor and after being told to wait on hold while they got me a supervisor, the same agent came back and told me that because the claim was closed that I could no longer speak to a supervisor regarding this issue.

I opened a U.S. Bank checking account in person at a branch because of a promotional bonus. I am a long-standing U.S. Bank customer and already maintain other personal and business accounts. I routinely complete well over five transactions on my existing accounts.

At the time of opening the new checking account, a material requirement of the promotion completing five transactions on the new account was not verbally disclosed to me. I relied on the bankers explanation when opening the account. Had this requirement been clearly disclosed, I would have completed it immediately. 

After the qualification period ended, I was informed that I was ineligible for the promotion solely because this requirement had not been met. This outcome resulted from a condition that was not clearly explained at account opening. 

I attempted to resolve this issue with branch staff, the branch manager, and the banks centralized resolution team. My clarification regarding the disclosure omission was formally added to the banks internal complaint record. However, the centralized team later confirmed that no remedy would be provided. 

Additionally, I operate two separate businesses and relied on this promotion when deciding where to place significant business funds. For my XXXX business, I deposited approximately {$25000.00} and maintained those funds in the account for over 60 days but did not receive the promotional bonus. I later opened another checking account for my XXXX XXXX business, deposited another approximately {$25000.00}, and again maintained the funds for over 60 days, yet the bonus was not provided. 

These deposits represent substantial business funds that were committed in good faith based on the expectation of the advertised promotion, resulting in additional financial impact. 

Due to this incomplete disclosure of a material term and the resulting financial harm, I respectfully request that U.S. Bank honor the promotional bonus or provide an equivalent goodwill credit.

text:
I am filing this complaint regarding my banks handling of multiple billing disputes. In XXXX separate disputes involving different merchants, my bank failed to conduct reasonable investigations, failed to request or meaningfully consider my evidence, and failed to provide required notice before reversing provisional credits. The same procedural failures occurred in both cases, indicating a pattern rather than an isolated error. 

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- I disputed a {$500.00} charge from a merchant for a scheduled service. I initially rescheduled the appointment and later canceled it. At the time of cancellation, the merchants representative informed me by phone that I would receive a full refund within XXXX business days. The representative specifically noted that the following Monday was a holiday and advised that the refund would likely be processed later in the following week. 

When the refund did not arrive within the timeframe they provided, I contacted the merchant again and was told someone would call me back. No one did. 

When I later followed up, the merchant stated they would not issue a refund due to a cancellation policy that had never been disclosed or mentioned previously, and directly contradicted the earlier verbal assurances that I would be refunded. 

I disputed this charge with my bank. The bank issued a provisional credit but did not contact me at any point during the investigation, did not request additional information, and did not allow me to respond to the merchants claims. The bank later denied the dispute based solely on the merchants assertion of a cancellation policy. 

I was told that a denial letter had been mailed on XX/XX/year>, but I never received it. I only became aware that the provisional credit was being reversed because I called the bank. Had I not called, the funds would have been removed from my account without my knowledge. 

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - I also disputed a charge of {$190.00} related to a subscription that auto-renewed. I believed auto-renew had been turned off months earlier. I received emails from the merchant with language stating that my subscription was about to expire, which reasonably signaled to me that auto-renewal was not active. 

After the charge occurred, I contacted the merchant directly. They stated the email language referred to something else and offered a partial refund. I initially declined but later accepted the partial refund. The partial refund was never issued. 

I then disputed the full amount with my bank and provided a screenshot of the email containing the misleading renewal language. Again, the bank did not contact me for additional information, did not allow me to respond to the merchants explanation, and completed the investigation without my knowledge. I only discovered the dispute had been denied by checking my account online and calling the bank, at which point I was told the provisional credit would be reversed the following week. 

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- In both disputes, the bank : - Failed to request or consider additional information from me - Relied solely on merchant statements- Completed investigations without my knowledge - Failed to provide timely and confirmed written notice of dispute denials- Reversed provisional credits without ensuring I was informed In both disputes, when I contacted the bank after seeing that the online dispute tracker showed the dispute as completed, I asked the representative for clear confirmation of XXXX points : whether the dispute had in fact been completed and what the decision was. Despite these direct questions, the representative continued to state that the dispute was still in progress and would not provide an answer. It was only after the representative placed me on hold after I requested a supervisor that I was told the dispute had been decided against me and that the merchant would not be refunding the charge. I then had to proactively ask whether the provisional credit would be withdrawn, at which point I was told that it would be. When I subsequently spoke with a supervisor, I was informed that the reversal was already scheduled for the following Monday. This conversation occurred on a Saturday, XXXX days prior to the reversal, and I was told there was nothing that could be done to prevent it. This further demonstrates that I was not provided timely or accurate notice of the dispute outcome and that adverse action was already scheduled before I was informed.

CFPB Complaint Potential UDAAP Violation Company : JPMorgan Chase Bank Product : Checking Account Issue : Account Closure Without Explanation Complaint : I am filing this complaint against JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding the sudden and unexplained closure of my checking account. I believe this action may constitute an Unfair, Deceptive, or Abusive Act or Practice ( UDAAP ) under the Consumer Financial Protection Act ( 12 U.S.C. 5531 ). On or about XX/XX/year>, I was notified that my checking account had been closed. No specific reason was provided. I was not given meaningful prior notice, an opportunity to respond, or any explanation sufficient to understand the basis for the decision. To my knowledge, my account was in good standing and I did not engage in fraudulent, suspicious, or unlawful activity. I just opened the account that day in branch. The banks failure to provide transparency regarding the closure : Prevents me from understanding or correcting any alleged issue. Disrupts my financial stability, including direct deposits and automatic payments. Potentially exposes me to reputational harm if negative information is reported to consumer reporting agencies. Under UDAAP standards, an act or practice is considered unfair if it causes or is likely to cause substantial injury to consumers that is not reasonably avoidable and not outweighed by countervailing benefits. Closing an account without explanation or due process may meet this standard, as consumers are left without clarity or recourse. Additionally, if the banks account agreement suggests fair treatment and transparency while failing to provide a reason for termination, such conduct may also be considered deceptive or abusive under federal consumer protection law. I respectfully request : A written explanation detailing the specific and factual basis for the account closure. Disclosure of whether any reports were made to XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, or other consumer reporting agencies, and copies of any such reports. Immediate release of any funds being held, including the legal basis for any hold. Written confirmation that no negative or adverse reporting has occurred, or correction of any inaccurate reporting. A review of this matter for potential UDAAP compliance concerns. I expect a formal written response addressing these issues in full.

Case Reference : PayPal Case ID XXXX Merchant : XXXX by XXXX Disputed Amount : {$130.00} Overview : This complaint challenges PayPal 's refusal to honor a Regulation E billing error and " Services Not Received '' claim. PayPal denied my appeal with the rationale that because the transaction occurred in-store, I " had the opportunity to ensure the correct delivery of your purchase. '' This reasoning is factually impossible and deceptive. 

1. Invalid " In-Store '' Defense for Service Failure : PayPal is applying " Card Present '' rulesintended for physical goods examined at a registerto a complex service migration ( Number Porting ). 

The Reality : A number port can not be " verified '' at the moment of payment. It is a back-end network process that failed days after I left the store. 

The Failure : The merchant ( XXXX ) failed to execute the " Port-In Promotion '' at the point of sale. This failure left my number in " limbo '' for nearly a week. 

The Result : Far from " ensuring delivery '' at the store, I was forced to travel between XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX locations for five days to fix XXXX 's error myself. The service I paid for was never delivered. 

2. Economic Damages & Double Payment : Because XXXX failed to provide the connectivity I paid for, I suffered direct economic damages beyond the original charge. 

I Paid Twice for One Month of Service : I paid XXXX {$130.00} for service I never received. To recover my phone number and have a working device, I was forced to pay a second carrier for that same month of service.

Unjust Enrichment : XXXX is currently retaining funds for a service period where they provided zero connectivity, while I was forced to pay a competitor to rectify their failure. 

3. The Billing Fraud ( Regulation E Violation ) : Regardless of the service failure, the transaction amount itself is fraudulent. 

The Charge : {$130.00}. 

The Receipt : The merchants own automated SMS receipt ( provided to PayPal ) confirms the total was only {$91.00}. 

The Violation : PayPals argument that I " accepted '' the charge by being in-store ignores the objective evidence of a {$43.00} unauthorized overcharge. A customer standing in a store can not physically prevent a merchant from keying in a hidden overcharge that contradicts the receipt generated moments later. 

Resolution Requested : PayPals assertion that an in-store presence absolves a merchant of delivering the correct service or charging the correct amount is a violation of consumer protection standards. 

I demand a full refund of {$130.00} for the non-delivered service and the " Port-In Promotion '' that was never executed.

I disputed a Discover credit card account that is reporting inaccurately on my credit report. XXXX responded stating the account was verified, however they failed to provide any documentation supporting the verification. text:
On or about XX/XX/year>, an incoming wire transfer was deposited into my Regions Bank account. The wire was legitimate, expected, and verifiable. I provided advance notice to the bank that the wire would occur and later provided full documentation proving the source of funds and my identity. 

More than a week after the wire was processed, Regions Bank placed a restriction on my account, preventing access to my funds. I immediately contacted the bank and was instructed to visit the branch. I went into the branch in person, presented government identification, and provided all requested documentation related to the wire. I was explicitly told by branch staff that the restriction would be lifted by lunchtime that same day. 

The restriction was not lifted. I did not receive a call back. Since that time, I have made repeated attempts to obtain basic information regarding my account status, including the reason for the restriction, confirmation that my documents were received, the department handling the matter, and an estimated timeline for resolution. 

Regions Bank phone representatives and a supervisor refused to provide any information and repeatedly stated that with this type of hold they could only refer me back to the branch. The branch, in turn, has stated they are waiting on a back office department and has provided no timeline or written explanation. As of today, no one at Regions Bank will provide me with any substantive information, despite my in-person visit and full cooperation. 

As a result of Regions Banks actions and lack of communication : I have been denied access to my own funds. 
I was given a specific resolution expectation that was not honored. 
I have been subjected to inconsistent and increasingly unprofessional communication. 
I am at risk of disruption to an IRS tax refund that is scheduled to be deposited into this account. 
I have been left without any written notice, explanation, or resolution timeline. 

I am not disputing Regions Banks right to conduct legitimate fraud or compliance reviews. I am disputing the banks failure to provide transparency, due process, timely resolution, or basic communication after documentation was provided and a same-day resolution was promised. 

I believe Regions Banks handling of this matter constitutes an unfair banking practice. A financial institution should not be able to indefinitely restrict access to customer funds without explanation, documentation, or a clear path to resolution.

text: To Whom It May Concern, I am submitting this complaint to request assistance regarding Discover Cards handling of a fraud dispute involving unauthorized transactions on my credit card account. Despite reporting the fraud promptly and providing supporting documentation, Discover has repeatedly closed the claim without adequately investigating the matter or resolving the unauthorized charges. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ) and Regulation Z, consumers are protected from liability for unauthorized credit card transactions and creditors are required to conduct a reasonable investigation when a billing error or fraud claim is reported. In my case, Discover failed to conduct a proper investigation and instead placed the burden on me to obtain information from the merchant. Background On XX/XX/XXXX, my Discover credit card was used fraudulently for a purchase with XXXX XXXX for {$90.00} I immediately reported the fraud to Discover and was instructed to discard the card while a replacement would be issued. I also activated the Discover Freeze/Lock feature * * in the mobile application to prevent further unauthorized activity. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received email notifications from Discover indicating that attempted purchases were blocked because my account was frozen, including two XXXX transactions of {$1400.00} each. Despite the account being frozen and despite Discover notifying me that the purchases were blocked, the charges were later processed and posted to my account. At that time : * My account was locked/frozen * I had not received the replacement credit card * I had not activated any replacement card * I did not authorize the transactions I immediately contacted Discover to report the transactions as fraud. Discovers Investigation Failures Discover opened a fraud claim but repeatedly closed the investigation citing an inability to reach the merchant ( XXXX ). Discover representatives advised that they could not reopen the claim unless I provided additional proof. This position is unreasonable and inconsistent with the requirements of the Fair Credit Billing Act. As the creditor, Discover is responsible for investigating unauthorized transactions and communicating with the merchant network. In order to assist Discover, I personally contacted XXXX multiple times via their customer support chat. XXXX representatives confirmed the following : * The airline tickets were booked fraudulently. * The tickets were cancelled and converted to travel bank credit. * The travel bank account was suspended due to fraud. * XXXX communicated the fraud findings and advised that Discover should process the refund. These communications are documented in the attached screenshots. Despite this information, Discover continued to close the fraud case and repost the charges to my account. In a later communication, Discover also stated that someone called claiming to be me and requested that the account be unfrozen. However, Discover could not explain how this individual successfully verified my identity or why no verification alerts were sent to me. My contact information has never changed, and I received no calls, verification codes, or authorization requests related to unfreezing the account. Financial Harm As a result of Discovers actions : * Fraudulent charges totaling {$1400.00} remain on my account. * My fraud claims have been repeatedly closed without resolution. * I have spent months attempting to coordinate communication between Discover and XXXX myself. * I have continued making minimum payments to avoid damage to my credit while this matter remains unresolved. Discover also issued correspondence stating they considered the transaction valid and would not continue the dispute despite the documentation provided. Security and Account Control Concerns A particularly concerning issue in this case is that the unauthorized transactions were processed while my Discover account was actively frozen using Discovers Freeze/Lock feature, which is specifically marketed to prevent new purchases if a card is lost or compromised. Discover even sent email notifications confirming that the XXXX transactions had been blocked because the account was frozen. However, those same transactions were later processed and posted to my account. This raises serious concerns about Discovers internal controls and the reliability of the account freeze feature that consumers rely on to prevent fraud. Furthermore, Discover later informed me that someone allegedly called and requested that the account be unfrozen. I dispute that I made such a call. Discover has not provided any documentation explaining : * How the callers identity was verified * What authentication methods were used * Why no alerts, calls, or verification notifications were sent to me * Why the account was unfrozen when the mobile application already allows the cardholder to perform that action directly If Discover allowed an unauthorized individual to unfreeze the account without proper identity verification, that represents a serious security failure and should not result in financial liability for the consumer. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau assist in resolving this matter and require Discover to : 1. Conduct a proper investigation of the unauthorized XXXX transactions. 2. Provide documentation showing how my account was allegedly unfrozen and how the callers identity was verified. 3. Coordinate directly with XXXX regarding the confirmed fraud investigation. 4. Remove the fraudulent XXXX charge from my account and reimburse the full unauthorized amount of {$1400.00}. 5. Correct any interest or fees related to the disputed charges. As a consumer who promptly reported fraud, secured my account, and cooperated fully with the investigation, I should not be held financially responsible for unauthorized transactions. I appreciate the CFPBs assistance in ensuring that Discover complies with its obligations under federal consumer protection laws. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Later that same evening, after I had already booked replacement travel, the merchant emailed stating that all flights were ticketed and confirmed. 

I disputed the {$750.00} charge with Bank of America on the basis of merchant misrepresentation and failure to provide services as represented. I provided a transcript of the recorded call showing that I was told additional payment was required and that I could not travel.

My complaint is that Bank of America failed to properly investigate the misrepresentation aspect of this dispute and instead focused solely on the refund policy.

text:
I am submitting this complaint regarding Goldman Sachs Bank USA, issuer of the Apple Card, and its handling of a billing dispute related to a merchant transaction. 

On XX/XX/2024, I made a purchase from XXXX in the amount of {$3000.00} using my Apple Card. At the time of purchase, the merchants return policy stated that items were eligible for a full refund if returned within 14 days of delivery, and I relied on this policy when completing the transaction. 

I received the merchandise on XX/XX/2024. Upon inspection, the garments had sensors still attached that could not be removed without damaging the items. I attempted to initiate a return in accordance with the merchants written instructions and the return policy in effect at the time of purchase. When I attempted to process the return on XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/2024, I was informed that the merchant had changed its return policy after my purchase and that the items were now considered non-refundable. 

I promptly filed a billing dispute with Goldman Sachs on XX/XX/2024. I provided supporting documentation, including screenshots of the merchants return policy as it appeared at the time of purchase, proof of delivery, receipts, photographs showing the sensors attached to the merchandise, records of my communications with the merchant, and additional materials reflecting other consumer complaints describing similar retroactive changes to the merchants return policy. Despite this documentation, Goldman Sachs denied the dispute and relied on the merchants updated return policy, which was implemented after my purchase. It does not appear that the dispute determinations evaluated the transaction under the return policy that governed the purchase date. 

Since that time, I have re-disputed this charge multiple times over the past year and have consistently received the same denial. 

I believe Goldman Sachs failed to conduct a reasonable investigation as required under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ). Allowing a merchant to apply a materially different return policy retroactively undermines consumer protections and results in cardholders being held responsible for charges that were disputed in good faith with supporting evidence. 

I am requesting that this matter be reviewed and that Goldman Sachs be required to properly investigate the dispute. I am seeking a refund of the {$3000.00} charge based on the merchants return policy as it existed at the time of purchase.

text: I submit this complaint as a victim of identity theft and unauthorized electronic fund transfers and as a final effort to resolve this matter before filing suit against Capital One Bank for violations of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ) and Regulation E. Approximately two years ago, my XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX came out of remission and I was diagnosed with a XXXX XXXX XXXX. I underwent XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and periods of medical incapacity while being evaluated for tXXXX XXXX During this time, my cellular telephones, financial accounts, computers, and personal identifying information were compromised and taken over without authorization. An individual identified as XXXX XXXX gained unauthorized access to my devices, financial information, and accounts and initiated unauthorized XXXX debits and electronic transfers involving Capital One accounts ending in XXXX, XXXX, and XXXX. Bank statements and correspondence were redirected away from my residence through unauthorized change-of-address activity, preventing discovery of the fraud while I remained critically ill and repeatedly hospitalized. I never authorized XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, or any other person to debit, transfer, withdraw, or otherwise access funds from my accounts from 2022 through the present date. XXXX XXXX likewise never authorized the disputed ACH debits or payment activity and never provided verbal, written, electronic, or any other authorization permitting my accounts to be debited. She is herself a victim of the same identity theft activity. Despite sworn affidavits, police reports, FTC Identity Theft Reports, medical documentation, and corroborating evidence establishing identity theft and lack of authorization, Capital One continues denying reimbursement and relies upon assumptions and speculation rather than competent evidence of authorization. Capital One does not possess and has never produced : Any signed ACH authorization ; Any authenticated electronic authorization ; Any recorded authorization ; Any authenticated device verification ; or Any competent evidence establishing knowing authorization for the disputed transactions. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693g, the burden rests entirely upon the financial institution to prove authorization for disputed electronic fund transfers. Regulation E further requires a reasonable, good-faith investigation once unauthorized transfers are reported. Other financial institutions, including XXXX and XXXX XXXX, investigated substantially similar fraudulent activity arising from the same identity theft events and reimbursed unauthorized transactions after determining the activity was fraudulent and unauthorized. Capital One instead continues victim blaming despite overwhelming evidence that I was critically ill, medically incapacitated, and the victim of widespread identity theft during the relevant periods. My circumstances fit squarely within the protections and extended look-back provisions applicable to victims of unauthorized electronic fund transfers and identity theft under federal law. The unauthorized activity was not reasonably discoverable while my accounts, devices, and communications remained compromised during prolonged medical incapacity. I request that the CFPB require Capital One to : 1. Reimburse all unauthorized ACH debits and electronic transfers ; 2. Cooperate in returning the unauthorized funds to my bank accounts ; 3. Refund all associated fees and charges ; 4. Correct any adverse credit reporting connected to the fraudulent activity ; 5. Provide all records relied upon in denying my disputes, including device logs, IP logs, authentication records, ACH authorizations, change-of-address records, and internal fraud investigation notes ; and 6. Comply fully with the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E. I attach sworn affidavits, police reports, FTC Identity Theft Reports, medical documentation, and supporting records establishing that the disputed transactions were unauthorized.
