This complaint concerns J.P. Morgan/Chases refusal or failure to provide a consistent online method for customers to add or update beneficiaries for certain account types ( checking, savings ), while providing digital beneficiary-management functionality for other account categories ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ). Chases own beneficiary FAQ states that a beneficiary can be added to a Chase account by visiting a branch, while its investment materials separately state that customers with J.P. Morgan XXXX XXXX investment accounts can designate or update beneficiaries through the Chase Mobile app or on chase.com. The result is a fragmented and burdensome process in which customers may be required to appear in person for some accounts, even though the institution already maintains secure digital channels for beneficiary updates for other products. This discrepancy creates unnecessary friction in basic account administration and undermines efficient estate planning for deposit-account holders and similarly situated consumers. These interactions imposed avoidable time, travel, scheduling, and administrative burdens for a task that should be manageable through authenticated digital banking channels. Chases own public materials show that online beneficiary management is available for certain investment accounts, which demonstrates that the bank already has the operational capability to support remote beneficiary maintenance in at least part of its product ecosystem. The inability to update beneficiaries online is not a minor convenience issue. Beneficiary designations help assets pass directly to designated individuals and can reduce the probability of a drawn-out probate process. When a customer can not promptly complete or revise those designations, estate planning may be delayed, family expectations may remain unclear, and account administration at death may become more complicated than necessary. This issue is especially serious when customers are XXXX, XXXX, traveling, working irregular hours, managing family emergencies, or otherwise unable to appear at a branch easily. Requiring an in-person visit for a routine beneficiary update creates a disproportionate burden when comparable financial servicing functions are commonly handled through secure online and mobile channels, and when Chase itself already permits digital beneficiary updates for J.P. Morgan XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. J.P. Morgan/Chase appears to maintain different servicing standards depending on account type : branch-based beneficiary changes for at least some Chase accounts, but digital self-service for certain investment accounts. If the institution can authenticate customers and process beneficiary changes online for one class of accounts, it should be able to explain clearly why similarly sensitive changes for ordinary consumer deposit accounts require branch attendance rather than secure digital workflows, identity verification, and electronic acknowledgment. In addition, J.P. Morgan asset-management materials indicate that beneficiary designations for some non-qualified and IRA accounts are handled through paper forms submitted by mail, further illustrating that the customer experience varies significantly across account types and may depend on legacy processing channels rather than modern digital convenience. From a consumer-protection perspective, such inconsistency can cause confusion, delay, and needless effort in an area closely tied to end-of-life planning and family financial security. Complaint Against Credit Card Issuer for Failure to Properly Investigate Billing Dispute Consumer Information Credit Card Issuer : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . ( Chase ) Transaction Amount : {$1800.00} Merchant : XXXX ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ) Service Type : Online educational course for a minor Dispute Type : Services not rendered as advertised / Misrepresentation Summary of the Issue I am filing this complaint due to Chases failure to conduct a fair, reasonable, and thorough investigation into a billing dispute involving misleading services and non-delivery as promised. Despite providing documentation and repeated explanations, Chase ruled in favor of the merchant without adequately reviewing the evidence or addressing the core issue of misrepresentation and non-performance. 
Detailed Explanation In reliance on advertisements viewed on XXXX, we enrolled our XXXX minor daughter in an XXXX online mathematics course offered by XXXX for {$1800.00}. The course was advertised as providing XXXX one-hour classes per month, focused on teaching innovative math techniques suitable for her age group. 
Prior to enrollment, XXXX explicitly assured us that : If the student did not understand the teacher, or If the class quality was not satisfactory, they would change the class or teacher, or allow cancellation with a refund. 
However, once classes began, the service delivered was materially different from what was advertised : Our daughter was placed in a class with significantly younger children, making the course inappropriate for her level. 
A substantial portion of class time was spent on unrelated personal discussions rather than instructional content. 
The instructor frequently faced internet and technical issues, resulting in students being unable to hear or follow the lesson. 
The effective instructional time was far less than the promised one hour per class. 
Due to these issues, we contacted XXXX multiple times via email and phone, requesting either : A change of class/teacher, or Cancellation and a refund XXXX representatives advised us not to attend the existing class and assured us that a new class and teacher would be assigned. Relying on this assurance, we waited. Despite repeated follow-ups, no new class was ever provided, and the service was neither corrected nor refunded. 
Eventually, when we requested formal cancellation and refund, XXXX failed to process either. 
Credit Card Dispute and Chases Failure to Investigate We then filed a dispute with Chase, providing : Written communications showing XXXX  assurances Evidence of repeated attempts to resolve the issue Explanation that services were not rendered as promised Chase ruled in favor of the merchant, stating : There was no way to determine whether the teacher quality was inadequate We were required to attend 30 classes before cancellation This decision is fundamentally flawed because : We were explicitly told not to attend further classes while awaiting reassignment We relied on the merchants representations in good faith Chase did not review or acknowledge our email evidence Chase failed to address the dispute as misrepresentation and non-delivery, focusing instead on attendance We made multiple attempts to explain this to Chases dispute team, but our concerns were repeatedly dismissed without substantive review or engagement. 
Basis for CFPB Complaint Chase failed to meet its obligations under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) by : Not conducting a reasonable investigation Ignoring relevant documentary evidence Accepting the merchants assertions without verification Mischaracterizing the dispute as subjective dissatisfaction rather than non-delivery of services Resolution Requested We respectfully request that : Chase reopen and properly investigate the dispute All submitted evidence be fully reviewed The charge of {$1800.00} be reversed, as the services were materially misrepresented and not delivered as promised We are seeking CFPBs assistance to ensure a fair and lawful resolution.

text:
This supplemental complaint concerns JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A.s issuance of a billing statement demanding payment for disputed balances while Chase simultaneously represents to the CFPB that the underlying disputes remain under active investigation. Issuing a demand for payment under these circumstances is improper, coercive, and incompatible with a lawful dispute process.

From the outset of this matter, the consumers disputes have been handled by Chases Executive Office, reflecting the seriousness of the issues raised. Despite Executive Office involvement from day one, Chase has repeatedly issued contradictory representationsasserting at various times that disputes were resolved, that investigations were ongoing, and that payment was duepositions that can not all be true at the same time. 

Since the first CFPB filing on XX/XX/year>, Chase has reversed provisional credits and rebilled disputed transactions totaling approximately {$91000.00}. These reversals culminated in the issuance of billing statements demanding payment while Chase continued to acknowledge that investigations were still ongoing and incomplete. 

The disputed transactions span multiple merchants. Chases failures are systemic and not limited to any single merchant. Chase failed to open disputes for all disputed transactions and failed to conduct lawful investigations across the full universe of merchants and charges at issue. Instead, Chase selectively opened only a portion of disputed cases, leaving a substantial number unacknowledged and uninvestigated. 

From XX/XX/year> to the present, Chase has issued numerous letters alleging that disputed transactions were valid, including after being placed on notice of ongoing consumer harm. These validity determinations were issued despite Chases failure to timely open and investigate all disputed transactions. 

Chases own actions confirm that no complete or lawful investigation existed when payment was demanded. Only approximately 20 % of disputed cases were initially opened, and hundreds of additional disputes were not opened until days 33 and 34 after the first CFPB filingwell beyond the required acknowledgment period. Nevertheless, Chase proceeded to rebill disputed amounts and demand payment.

Despite repeated notice of ongoing consumer harm, Chase has continued to issue billing statements demanding payment, furnish credit reporting reflecting inflated balances and utilization, and maintain adverse account status. Each day the disputed balances remain reported, the consumers credit continues to deteriorate. To date, this has resulted in a cumulative 29-point decline in the consumers credit score, with harm continuing daily.

The consumer is not, and has never been, in settlement discussions with any merchant. The consumer did not solicit merchant contact and will not entertain settlement discussions. Responsibility for dispute investigation, billing accuracy, and credit reporting rests solely with Chase as the card issuer.

Chase has been repeatedly placed on noticethrough CFPB complaints handled by its Executive Office and direct communicationsof ongoing consumer harm. Rather than halt adverse actions, Chase has continued and escalated retaliatory conduct, including rebilling, demands for payment, adverse credit reporting, and account actions, compounding harm while investigations remain unresolved.

This complaint concerns Citibank, N.A.s failure to properly investigate a billing error involving duplicate charges, and Citibanks subsequent mischaracterization of the dispute to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau.

SUMMARY OF THE BILLING ERROR On XX/XX/XXXX, two identical charges posted to my Citibank account from the same merchant ( XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ) for the same amount, on the same date, seconds apart. These charges are objectively duplicate transactions resulting from a merchant card-reader malfunction. I did not authorize two separate credit-card charges.

Under the Fair Credit Billing Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1666 ), this constitutes a single billing error consisting of two duplicate transactions.

CITIBANKS IMPROPER HANDLING Citibank created two internal dispute reference numbers for the duplicate charges. One dispute remains open. The second dispute was closed without investigation, not because the charge was valid, but solely due to an initial dispute category selection ( alternative payment method ) that referenced the fact that I paid the merchant in cash.

Citibank elevated internal labeling over statutory duty and failed to investigate both duplicate transactions, as required by the FCBA and Regulation Z. A billing error can not be denied or dismissed based on how a consumer initially labels a dispute when the underlying facts clearly establish a duplicate charge.

MISCHARACTERIZATION TO THE CFPB In responding to my prior CFPB complaint, Citibank represented that only one dispute exists and remains open, omitting the fact that : Two duplicate charges posted ; One duplicate charge was closed without investigation ; and The billing error, as defined by statute, was not fully investigated.

This representation is inaccurate and misleading, because the FCBA governs billing errors, not internal dispute ticketing. Investigating only one of two duplicate transactions does not satisfy Citibanks statutory obligations.

NOTICE TO CITIBANK On XX/XX/XXXX, I sent Citibank a written correction letter formally notifying it that : Both charges are duplicates ; Closing one dispute based on categorization violates FCBA standards ; and Citibank must investigate and resolve both transactions or permanently reverse the duplicate charges.

Citibank has not corrected the error.

ONGOING HARM As a result of Citibanks conduct : A conditional credit was reversed without a complete investigation ; My account balance remains inaccurate ; and I face continued risk of improper credit reporting and collection activity. 

RELIEF REQUESTED I respectfully request that the CFPB require Citibank to : Acknowledge that this matter involves one billing error consisting of two duplicate transactions Reopen or substantively investigate the second duplicate charge Permanently reverse the duplicate charge unless Citibank can produce evidence of two separate authorizations Correct the CFPB record to accurately reflect the nature of the billing error This new complaint is filed because I was advised by a CFPB representative that the prior complaint could not be amended to correct Citibanks mischaracterization or to add supplemental documentation

On XX/XX/year>, I made a single authorized online purchase of {$29.00} from a website that appeared legitimate. This was the only transaction I approved.

Within the next 48 hours, the same merchant processed approximately 15 additional online charges totaling about {$7500.00}, even though my credit limit was {$3800.00}. I did not authorize any of these additional charges. I did not consent to recurring billing, incremental charges, subscriptions, or any amounts beyond the original {$29.00}.

I promptly contacted my bank and reported the charges as fraud. The bank rejected the fraud claim, stating they should instead be treated as billing disputes. I followed the banks instructions and re-filed all 15 transactions as billing disputes, and separately disputed the original {$29.00} charge as goods/services not received, since nothing was ever delivered. 

During the billing dispute process, the bank has repeatedly requested documentation that can not exist for unauthorized transactions ( such as invoices, contracts, or receipts for the fraudulent charges ). I have consistently explained that : * The additional charges were not authorized * There is no merchandise or service associated with those charges * There are no invoices or receipts because I did not make those purchases Despite this, the bank has continued to delay resolution and, has erroneously deducted the disputed {$29.00} amount from 3 of the larger claims, even though the {$29.00} charge is itself under a separate dispute and has not been resolved or credited. It has has rejected one of my billing disputes.

The bank has stated it may take up to 45 days to respond to the billing disputes. Meanwhile, I am concerned that the bank has mishandled the investigation by : * Misclassifying fraud as billing disputes, * Allowing charges far above my credit limit, * Treating unauthorized charges as if they were valid purchases, and * Making accounting errors during the dispute process.

I am requesting CFPB assistance to ensure the bank properly investigates these unauthorized charges, applies applicable consumer protections, corrects its errors, and credits the disputed amounts.

My items were not personalized or custom. Despite this, my order did not ship within the timeframe represented at purchase. By XX/XX/XXXX, nearly XXXX month later, the order still had not shipped, so I contacted the merchant to follow up. On XX/XX/XXXX, the merchant responded that they were investigating the delay, and I separately received a shipment confirmation email on that day ( XX/XX/XXXX ) more than five weeks after purchase. The merchant did not provide a meaningful opportunity to cancel the order despite this substantial delay. I understand that when merchandise can not be shipped within the promised timeframe, merchants are expected to provide notice and a meaningful option to cancel. That did not occur here. After the order finally arrived, I promptly requested a return on XX/XX/XXXX. The merchant did not process the return request nor communicate with me at all. I followed up again on XX/XX/XXXX because I still had not received information necessary to complete the return. The merchant then refused to provide a refund to my original payment method and instead limited me to store credit only. I disputed this transaction with XXXX because the goods were not provided as agreed and the merchant did not offer an adequate refund remedy after a substantial shipping delay. In response to the dispute, the merchant submitted only a generic copy of its shipping and return policy ( provided by XXXX at my request ). XXXX accepted that policy language as sufficient and denied my dispute in a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX. I then requested continued review and provided additional information, but XXXX again denied the dispute in a final letter dated XX/XX/XXXX. Specifically, I requested they review this as a " goods not delivered as promised '' issue ( they had internally classified as " goods not delivered '' ), but they did not do this. The merchant did not comply with its obligations in my specific transaction. XXXX did not require or evaluate transaction-specific evidence showing : ( XXXX ) why a non-personalized order that was represented as shipping in XXXX business days was delayed until XX/XX/XXXX ( XXXX ) whether I was provided a meaningful option to cancel after the significant delay ( XXXX ) why the merchant refused a refund and restricted me to store credit only, despite requesting a cancellation due to their delayed delivery Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, I understand that card issuers are required to conduct a reasonable investigation of disputed charges. In this case, XXXX appears to have relied on generic merchant policy language rather than transaction-specific evidence, and therefore did not conduct a reasonable investigation.

Between late XXXX and XXXX XXXX, I made multiple purchases of academic and professional textbooks across separate orders from two merchants operating under the names XXXX and XXXX. The total amount paid was approximately {$83000.00}, consisting of approximately {$60000.00} to XXXX and {$23000.00} to XXXX. 

XXXX transactions appeared on my Chase account as XXXX charges, although several of those transactions do not appear within my XXXX account history. All XXXX transactions were processed directly through my Chase debit card. 

At the time of purchase, both merchants represented themselves as legitimate U.S.-based sellers offering authentic textbooks. I relied on these representations and believed the books were genuine, authorized, and manufactured and distributed in accordance with publisher standards.

After delivery, I discovered multiple issues that were not disclosed at the time of purchase. Many shipments lacked tracking information, some items were missing, and shipping labels and tracking data showed that the books originated from XXXX. This international sourcing was never disclosed on the merchants websites or during checkout. 

Upon inspection, the books exhibited multiple indicators of inauthenticity, including irregular binding, printing inconsistencies, and other physical characteristics inconsistent with legitimate editions. These issues were discovered only after delivery. 

I contacted the merchants regarding missing items and authenticity concerns. XXXX stated they would investigate but failed to issue refunds for missing books. Instead, they attempted to ship replacement books significantly later and asserted the books were authentic. As part of this response, XXXX provided an invoice from an overseas book binding house in XXXX as purported proof of legitimacy. 

I then contacted multiple publishers directly, including the National Fire Protection Association ( NFPA ), and received written confirmation that their publications are printed exclusively in the United States and that they do not authorize printing, binding, or manufacturing of their books outside the U.S., nor do they work with overseas binding houses for these titles.

Additionally, I obtained independent second opinions from multiple established book and resale businesses, including XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and The XXXX XXXX. Each independently identified physical indicators consistent with inauthentic or improperly manufactured books. 

Based on this evidence, the goods I received were materially different from what was represented and raise serious concerns of misrepresentation and potential counterfeit merchandise. The transactions were authorized only because of false representations regarding authenticity, origin, and legitimacy, which were discovered after delivery. 

I reported these transactions to Chase and requested a full investigation into the disputed debit card charges, providing extensive documentation including publisher confirmations, expert opinions, photographs, shipping records, and merchant communications. Despite this, the transactions were deemed authorized, and I was held financially responsible. 

I am filing this complaint because these charges resulted from fraudulent misrepresentation, and I believe Chase failed to properly evaluate evidence demonstrating that the transactions were induced by deception and should not have been treated as validly authorized debit card transactions. 

In addition, multiple orders contained serious shipping irregularities. For example, one order ( XXXX ) was provided a XXXX tracking number that XXXX later confirmed was invalid and did not exist. In another order ( XXXX ), the merchants website displayed invalid XXXX tracking numbers, but a later email from the merchant provided a different XXXX  tracking number that showed shipment originating from XXXX. These inconsistencies and undisclosed foreign origins were only discovered after payment and are inconsistent with the merchants representations and the terms of the transaction.

text: Product or service : Bank account / deposit account checking Date of incident : XX/XX/year> Check number : XXXX Check amount : {$9100.00} Source of check : XXXX Bank What happened? On XX/XX/year>, I deposited check number XXXX in the amount of {$9100.00} into my Bank of America XXXX XXXX Banking account ( ending in XXXX ) at a Bank of America ATM located at a Bank of America XXXX XXXX. Despite this deposit, Bank of America placed an unauthorized and improperly disclosed hold on these funds. Bank of America has provided contradictory explanations regarding this hold. In their written response to my XX/XX/year>, CFPB inquiry, the bank stated : 1. The funds were made available in my account on XX/XX/year> ( the same day as the deposit ) ; 2. Yet the bank simultaneously stated that it had placed a " temporary hold '' on the deposit " to protect both you and the bank in the event the check was returned unpaid. '' These two statements are logically contradictory. A hold, by definition, restricts access to deposited funds. If the funds were truly available on XX/XX/XXXX, then there was no hold and my complaint was entirely unfounded. If a hold was placed, then I was deprived of timely access to my funds, and the bank 's denial of my reimbursement request is unjustified. What specific harm did this cause? The hold on my funds caused immediate and actual financial harm because I was unable to access or use the {$9100.00} deposit when I needed it. Additionally, the bank 's contradictory responses have made it impossible for me to understand what actually happened to my deposit, and the bank has refused to provide any compensation for the harm caused by the hold.Bank of America 's conduct appears to violate the Expedited Funds Availability Act ( EFAA ), as implemented by Regulation CC ( 12 CFR 229 ). Regulation CC sets forth specific time schedules that banks must follow when making deposited funds available to consumers, and requires banks to clearly disclose their funds availability policies. The EFAA was enacted to reduce the time that banks could hold deposited checks, and Regulation CC establishes federal standards for when banks must make deposited funds available and how hold policies must be disclosed. Bank of America 's contradictory statements regarding this deposit suggest that the bank either : 1. Placed an unauthorized hold without proper disclosure, in violation of Regulation CC ; or 2. Made the funds available as required, in which case the bank 's initial hold was improper and the bank 's refusal to explain what occurred constitutes a deceptive practice. Either way, Bank of America 's conduct has caused actual financial harm to me and has failed to provide the transparency required by federal consumer financial protection laws.

text: CFPB Complaint Bank of America Wire Fraud Case Company : Bank of America Issue : Fraud / Unauthorized Transfers/ Scam ( XXXX XXXX ) Complaint : On XX/XX/year>, at approximately XXXXXXXX XXXX, I received a phone call from individuals impersonating Bank of Americas fraud department. The call lasted nearly three hours. During this time, I was manipulated through sophisticated social engineering tactics into initiating three wire transfers totaling {$40000.00}. This incident did not occur in isolation. In the three weeks leading up to this event, I had already been in direct contact with Bank of Americas legitimate fraud department on two separate occasions due to unauthorized debit card activity. A replacement card had been issued, yet fraudulent activity continued even before I received it. During one of those legitimate calls, a Bank of America representative advised that changing my account number might be necessary to secure my funds. The scammers used this exact context to gain my trust. They referenced fraudulent activity, asked security-style questions, and demonstrated knowledge of my account balances. I was then transferred to another individual who instructed me, step-by-step, within my Bank of America mobile app , to move my funds into what I was told were secure accounts while new account numbers were being generated. The caller explained that the account names appearing during the transfers were temporary internal designations and that the system would update within 48 hours. He also stated he would follow up with me to confirm completion. Before each transfer, he read disclosures that sounded consistent with legitimate bank procedures. Based on my recent legitimate interactions with Bank of Americas fraud department, the callers apparent knowledge of my accounts, the use of Bank of Americas own mobile platform, and the urgency tied to ongoing fraud on my account, I reasonably believed I was acting under the direction of Bank of America to protect my funds. Additionally, shortly after completing the transfers, I contacted Bank of America directly to confirm that the transactions had been completed, as I had been instructed that the process would take a couple of days and that I would receive a follow-up call that Friday. During this call, I asked the representative to verify the status of the transfers. The representative appeared alarmed and informed me that Bank of Americas fraud department does not schedule or conduct outbound follow-up calls of that nature. However, I had been told during the earlier interaction that a callback was scheduled, and my call records reflected a scheduled follow-up. That follow-up call did occur on the expected day, but when I answered, there was no response on the line. Later that same day, I contacted Bank of America directly and was informed that no such call had taken place and that the wire transfers were fraudulent. I immediately reported the incident and fully cooperated with the bank. However, Bank of America has since closed my claims after recovering only {$2200.00} total, leaving the vast majority of the {$40000.00} unrecovered. I am disputing this outcome. This was not a voluntary transaction in the traditional sense. I was deceived into acting under the belief that I was securing my funds through Bank of Americas fraud department during an active fraud situation on my account. Requested Resolution : A full reinvestigation of my claim A detailed explanation of how these transactions were determined to be authorized Documentation of any wire recall attempts and recovery efforts Consideration of reimbursement due to the fraudulent inducement and impersonation involved A review of whether adequate safeguards were in place given my recent fraud alerts and account activity I believe this situation warrants further review, as it involves impersonation of the bank, exploitation of an active fraud case, and manipulation through the banks own systems.

text: I am filing a formal complaint regarding unauthorized debit card transactions on my JPMorgan Chase account. These unauthorized transactions persisted continuously from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX. In approximately XX/XX/XXXX, my original debit card was stolen. I reported the card as lost to Chase, and a replacement card was issued. Despite this, unauthorized XXXX transactions began appearing on XX/XX/XXXX, using the replacement card. These transactions continued through XX/XX/XXXX and were processed in XXXX pesos ( XXXX ). I have never been to XXXX during this period and did not authorize these charges. I reviewed my XXXX account and confirmed there are no corresponding trips or activity. All of my legitimate XXXX usage is within the United States, charged in USD, and linked to a different payment method. I do not use my debit card for XXXX transactions. The fraudulent charges consist of repeated XXXX transactions in XXXX, along with foreign exchange conversion fees, forming a consistent pattern across months. CRITICAL ISSUE NOT REASONABLY IDENTIFIABLE EARLIER : When the fraud began in XX/XX/XXXX, the transactions appeared as small XXXX charges intermixed with normal activity. Because XXXX is a merchant I legitimately use, these charges did not immediately appear suspicious. Additionally, the foreign nature of the transactions was not clearly obvious, as the XXXX currency and exchange rates were embedded within transaction details. The activity consisted of multiple low-value transactions rather than a single large suspicious charge. Only over time did a recognizable pattern emerge, including repeated foreign transactions, increasing frequency, and the absence of these transactions in my XXXX account. This was therefore a gradual and continuous fraud pattern that could not reasonably be identified at the beginning. BANK ACCOUNTABILITY AND FAILURE TO DETECT PATTERN : Chase was already aware of a prior card compromise when my original card was reported stolen and replaced. Despite this, the replacement card began showing repeated foreign XXXX transactions shortly afterward. These transactions followed a clear, repetitive pattern with consistent merchant, currency, and structure. The activity continued for an extended period without being flagged, blocked, or escalated by the bank. Financial institutions promote their fraud detection systems, yet this extended pattern of foreign activity went undetected and unflagged. CRITICAL ISSUE CONTINUOUS FRAUD SCHEME ( NOT ISOLATED TRANSACTIONS ) : The unauthorized transactions in this case must be evaluated as one continuous fraud scheme, rather than separate or isolated incidents. All transactions share the same characteristics : the same merchant ( XXXX ), the same foreign currency ( XXXX ), identical structure, absence from my XXXX account, and inconsistency with my normal behavior. This pattern persisted continuously from XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, without interruption. There are no meaningful differences between earlier and later transactions. The only difference being applied by the bank is timing, not substance. These transactions represent a single, ongoing unauthorized fraud scheme affecting the same account and payment method. Treating these as separate events ignores the clear continuity and results in inconsistent outcomes. Financial institutions are expected to identify repeated patterns and treat related activity consistently. However, Chase has reimbursed some transactions while denying others that are identical in every material way. Given the consistent and uninterrupted nature of these transactions, they must be treated as part of a single continuous fraud scheme and not as independent transactions. INCONSISTENT TREATMENT OF IDENTICAL TRANSACTIONS : Chase has already acknowledged that some of these transactions are unauthorized by issuing partial reimbursement. However, earlier transactions with identical patterns were denied. These transactions should be treated consistently as part of the same fraud case. The evidence demonstrates a continuous pattern of unauthorized foreign transactions that were not reasonably identifiable at the outset and must be treated as a single fraud scheme. PS : I have attached my bank statements where all the fraudulent transaction is marked, XXXX XXXX option page showing credit cards ( not the compromised debit card ) linked to my XXXX account, a spending summary and the PDF of the formal complaint and the fair resolution requested. Thanks.

I am submitting this complaint regarding a deferred interest charge applied to my CareCredit credit card account with Synchrony Bank.

I am enrolled in paperless statements and have consistently made my monthly payments on time. I manage my account by ensuring payments are made as required. While the company may have sent electronic communications, I am not a technology-oriented consumer and do not regularly use or monitor email. I rely on clear, prominent disclosures within my account statements and direct explanations to understand important account changes. There was no clear, conspicuous notification within my statements or account summary explaining that this large retroactive interest charge would be applied if the balance was not paid in full by a specific date, or clearly identifying when the promotion would expire. There should be a notice on your online account that also tells you when this " promotion '' will expire as well as they have it stated on the statements they send out to customers via mail and email. That would be the just thing to do to give the customer a FAIR chance at not having retroactive interest charged as well as it would allow the company 100 % chance to tell the customer that they did everything in their power to make the customer aware of the promotion expiration date as well as interest rate that would be charged if the balance wasn't paid in full. In addition, there were XXXX separate purchases made and nowhere on the online payment portal is there a distinction between the XXXX to know which balance needs to be paid prior to which expiration date to avoid this colossal interest charge all at once. 

Had I been clearly informed or reminded of the promotional expiration date and the consequences of not paying the balance in full, I would have paid the balance before the promotion ended. My goal has never been to carry interest or pay more money, but without clear information, it is impossible for a customer to make an informed decision to avoid retroactive interest charges. 

Additionally, I currently have another promotional balance on my account that is approaching expiration, which further highlights the importance of transparent and proactive communication from the lender.

I believe it is unfair that Synchrony Bank does not offer a reasonable customer solution in situations like this, such as a one-time courtesy adjustment where, upon discovering the deferred interest and being willing to pay the remaining balance in full, the retroactive interest charge could be removed. I am willing to pay the promotional balance in full immediately, but I am requesting that the {$900.00} deferred interest charge be removed and reversed as it was not clearly disclosed or reasonably noticeable. 

I am requesting that Synchrony Bank review this matter and provide a fair resolution by removing the deferred interest charge as a courtesy adjustment based on lack of clear disclosure, my positive payment history, and my good-faith intent to avoid interest.

text: I. Victim of Mail Theft and Identity Theft I am a victim of identity theft involving stolen mail and unauthorized use of my financial information. Their communication stated that XXXX had been notified and would be sending a technician to repair the broken slots, and confirmed that XXXX has sole jurisdiction over mailbox security and delivery. This condition was outside of my control, as XXXX retains sole jurisdiction over mailbox security and repairs, and residents can not access or secure these units. This establishes that the mailbox breach was a documented service failure involving a federal mail system, not a privately secured mailbox. As a result of this breach, my mail was stolen, including a replacement Barclays credit card and a full Equifax credit report containing sensitive personal information. I reported this incident to the United States Postal Service on XX/XX/year> ( Service Request No. XXXX ), which was subsequently escalated and accepted by the United States XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX Case No. XXXX ). I also filed an identity theft report with the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC Report XXXX. XXXX ) and a police report with the XXXX Police Department ( Report XXXX. XXXX ). XXXX. XXXX, Fraud Notification, and Immediate Reporting On XX/XX/year>, Barclays Fraud Detection Unit identified activity on my account that XXXX be related to fraudulent usage and created a fraud case ( Case # XXXX ) before I had contacted them, instructing me to verify the activity. This notification originated from Barclays Fraud Detection Unit and provided a direct contact number, which I used to respond. I contacted Barclays and completed a full review of the account activity with their representative. During that call, I clearly stated that I did not authorize any of the XX/XX/XXXX transactions, including the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX charge, the XXXX charge, and all related attempted transactions. The representative identified a prior charge dated XX/XX/year> for {$40.00} ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ). I stated that I was unsure of that transaction and would verify it separately. This was not reported as part of the XX/XX/XXXX unauthorized activity. On XX/XX/year>, I confirmed that the XX/XX/XXXX XXXX charge was legitimate and contacted Barclays to clarify that it was valid and unrelated to the fraud incident. Barclays did not request supporting documentation from me as part of its investigation. I provided all documentation voluntarily, including my police report, statement of facts, and supporting evidence, in an effort to assist in identifying the individual responsible. On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a written statement of facts and supporting documentation by fax, along with a police-signed identity theft transaction records request. On XX/XX/year> at approximately XXXX PM, I submitted a formal appeal by fax to Barclays XXXX XXXX department, requesting reconsideration of their fraud determination. This appeal included the police narrative, supporting documentation, and previously submitted evidence, including images of the damaged mailbox, missing mail, and XXXX XXXX XXXX records. XXXX. Complete Transaction Sequence and Pattern of XXXX The XX/XX/year> incident consisted of a single, continuous sequence of XXXX transactions within a short period of time. This included : XXXX approved transactions totaling {$80.00} XXXX declined transactions totaling {$2300.00} XXXX attempted exposure of {$2400.00} Barclays XXXX show that the replacement card was activated on XX/XX/year> at approximately XXXX PM. I did not receive, possess, or activate this card at any time. The unauthorized transaction sequence began immediately after this activation. The sequence began with a {$6.00} charge at XXXX in the XXXX, followed immediately by XXXX declined XXXX transactions of {$200.00} each. Despite this activity already being declined, a {$74.00} XXXX charge was then approved. The sequence then escalated to high-value cash withdrawal and cash advance attempts, including {$1000.00} and {$500.00} withdrawal attempts at XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX and XXXX {$300.00} cash advance attempt at CVS Pharmacy XXXX XXXX with additional declined digital transfer and online purchase attempts from XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX, and XXXX. Further failed attempts continued through approximately XXXX PM. This was not isolated activity, but a continuous pattern of attempted use during a single incident. XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX Barclays identified and responded to this activity by initiating a fraud case ( Case # XXXX ), closing the account, and issuing a replacement card with a new account number. These actions show that Barclays treated the activity as fraud when it happened. However, Barclays later changed its position and decided that XXXX transactions from that same sequence were valid and that I benefited from them. Barclays has not explained how the same activity they identified as fraud, closed the account for, and required me to verify can later be treated as authorized charges that I am responsible for. Barclays also has not explained how the first and fourth transactions in this sequence were considered authorized while the immediately surrounding transactions were declined and part of the same pattern of fraudulent activity. V. Omission of XXXX Transactions and Incomplete Investigation I reported all XXXX transactions from XX/XX/year> as unauthorized and documented them in my statement of facts, which was provided to law enforcement and Barclays. However, Barclays XX/XX/year> correspondence referenced only XXXX transactions and did not include the XXXX declined transactions from the same sequence. Subsequent determinations dated XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX addressed only the approved transactions and the XX/XX/XXXX XXXX charge, while continuing to omit the remaining XXXX transactions entirely. Barclays has not explained what consideration was given to these XXXX transactions, why they were excluded from the investigation, or why they are no longer reflected in my account records. The activity on XX/XX/year>, including attempted ATM withdrawals, cash advances, and rapid transaction activity in a different location, is not consistent with my normal account usage. I have no history of ATM withdrawals or similar activity on this account. VI. Continued Investigation of a Resolved Transaction Despite my clarification on XX/XX/year> and again in my XX/XX/year> submission that the XX/XX/XXXX XXXX transaction was valid and unrelated, Barclays continued to investigate that charge and issued a determination on XX/XX/year> stating that it was valid based on merchant documentation. Failure to Provide Records On XX/XX/year>, I submitted a formal request for records pursuant to California XXXX XXXX XXXX, including a police-signed identity theft transaction records request, seeking all records related to the unauthorized use of my account, including activation data, device or IP information, transaction logs, and ATM or terminal records. XXXX Liability and Consumer Protection Under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Mastercards XXXX Liability Policy, I am not responsible for unauthorized transactions where I did not authorize the activity, did not receive the card, and reported the activity promptly. XXXX. Conclusion Barclays determination is incomplete, inconsistent, and unsupported by the full set of facts. The activity was treated as fraud at the time it occurred, involved a continuous sequence of XXXX transactions, and resulted in account closure and reissuance of a new account number. Barclays later reversed its position without addressing the full transaction pattern, the omitted transactions, or the supporting documentation provided. Instead, they relied solely on the fact that services were completed. I am requesting that Chase : 1. Reconsider this dispute under the correct framework whether the transaction constituted valid payment to the merchant 2. Address the evidence that the payment was misdirected due to fraud and did not reach the intended recipient 3. Provide a clear explanation of how a payment sent to a third party due to fraud can be considered valid payment for services rendered For context, another card issuer reviewing a related transaction has reopened the dispute and issued conditional credit based on the same underlying facts, indicating that this situation warrants further review. I am filing this complaint regarding what I believe to be misleading and deceptive financing practices associated with a store credit account issued by Comenity Capital Bank for a purchase made at XXXX. Approximately XXXX year and XXXX months ago, I made a purchase at a XXXX store and opened a credit account through Comenity Capital Bank to finance the purchase. At the time of the transaction, the store representative informed me that my minimum monthly payment would be about {$54.00}. I was also told that if I paid approximately {$100.00} per month, the balance would be paid off within the year and I would avoid any interest charges. Based on this explanation, the promotion was clearly presented to me as an interest-free loan for one year as long as I followed the recommended payment amount. Relying on this information, I enrolled in automatic payments and paperless billing and consistently made my payments on time. However, after the promotional period passed by approximately one month, I discovered that {$710.00} in deferred interest had been added to my account on a remaining balance of {$900.00}. When I contacted Comenity Capital Bank, I was informed that because the balance had not been fully paid by the promotional deadline, all interest for the entire year had been retroactively applied. This was the first time it was clearly explained to me that the promotion functioned as a deferred-interest agreement rather than a simple interest-free promotion. The information provided at the store led me to believe that following the recommended payment plan would allow me to avoid interest charges. Had the terms been clearly explainedthat the full balance had to be completely paid before the deadline or all accumulated interest would be appliedI would have ensured the balance was paid in full before that date. Additionally, when I requested copies of my contract and disclosures regarding the promotional period, I was told they were only available online because I was enrolled in paperless billing. My request to have these documents mailed to me was refused. I believe the promotional financing was misrepresented at the time of purchase and that the explanation provided by the sales representative created the impression that the financing would remain interest-free if I followed the payment guidance given to me, which I did. I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed and that the {$710.00} deferred interest charge be reconsidered or removed so I can resolve the remaining principal balance. I am also concerned that the promotional financing may have been misrepresented at the point of sale. The explanation provided by the sales associate created the clear impression that making the recommended monthly payments would allow the balance to be paid within the year and prevent interest charges. At no point was it clearly explained that the promotion functioned as a deferred-interest agreement where all interest for the entire year would be retroactively applied if the balance was not fully paid by the promotional deadline. Because this critical condition was not clearly disclosed to me during the purchase, I believe I may have been misled about the true nature of the financing terms. I respectfully request a full review of this matter and a goodwill adjustment removing the {$710.00} deferred interest so that I may resolve the remaining principal balance promptly.

text:
On XX/XX/XXXX, I contacted XXXX only to inquire whether they could ask XXXX if a free cancellation with a full refund might be possible due to the airlines schedule change. This was an inquiry, not a request to cancel. XXXX said they would contact XXXX on my behalf, but I received no response for several days. 

Because I never intended to cancel my ticket, on XX/XX/XXXX, I formally withdrew any cancellation status and made it clear that I was keeping my ticket. This is documented in the attachment titled No Cancellation ( PDF ), which shows my explicit communication with XXXX confirming that I was not canceling and that I intended to retain the booking. 

After that, I initiated a dispute because the itinerary had been unilaterally altered and the service I purchased was no longer usable. 

Important clarification : In Capital Ones dispute workflow, I misunderstood the meaning of the cancel/cancellation option. I entered the date of my inquiry to XXXX ( XX/XX/XXXX ) about whether a free cancellation might be possible. That date reflects only my inquiry, not my intent to cancel and not a cancellation request. I never agreed to cancel my ticket. 

On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX contacted me and stated that I would need to pay again in order to keep my ticket. I had never received any full refund. There was no legal or factual basis for requiring me to pay a second time for the same ticket. I refused to make a second payment and clearly stated in writing that I did not agree to any cancellation and that I rejected XXXX canceling my ticket. This is shown in XXXX Important Information regarding XXXX XXXX XXXX Ticket number XXXX ( PDF ). 

After I refused to pay a second time, XXXX canceled my ticket anyway, despite my explicit objection. The booking no longer exists in XXXX system, and XXXX shows no active record. XXXX has also confirmed that the ticket can not be restored even though the money has been taken from me. The transportation service I paid for no longer exists. 

Requiring a second payment to keep a ticket that had already been fully paid for, and then canceling that ticket when I refused, is not a valid basis to treat the original charge as delivered service. 

Capital One closed my dispute by relying on the merchants statement that no cancellation per policy was received, as shown in XXXX. My case was effectively treated as consumer-cancelled merchandise or service. This classification is factually wrong. I did not cancel. I only inquired about whether a free cancellation might be possible, then explicitly withdrew any cancellation status and objected in writing. 

The real issue is that the merchant unilaterally canceled the service against my will after demanding a second payment for a ticket I had already paid for and had not been refunded. This case should be treated as Service Not Rendered / Merchant Canceled the Service, not as a failed cancellation of a non-refundable ticket. Capital One did not meaningfully investigate these facts and instead accepted the merchants cancellation as if it were my own choice.

text: PRODUCT : Credit card ISSUE : Problem during the application process - confusing or misleading advertising/marketing COMPANY : JPMorgan Chase Bank , N.A . I did not knowingly apply for this product and had no business case for doing so, as my explicit goal was to secure an introductory 0 % APR. The reason for this confusion is clear : the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX and Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX are presented with nearly identical visual designs. Both cards are dark blue. Both use the same " XXXX XXXX '' branding and typography. Both have the same chip placement and Chase logo treatment. The only visual distinction during the online application process is a single word ( " Preferred '' vs. " Unlimited '' ) and a barely perceptible difference in shade of blue. These products appear on the same Chase business credit card landing page, side by side. Because I believed I had a 0 % introductory APR card, I used it to fund standard business expenses and set the account to autopay the minimum, consistent with standard 0 % introductory cash flow management. At no point during the months of use did any Chase communication, statement design, or account notification make it obvious that I was being charged interest. The interest accrued silently in the background. On XX/XX/XXXX, my Chase dashboard showed a balance of {$15000.00} on a {$21000.00} limit. The account continued accruing interest. On approximately XX/XX/XXXX, charges on the card began declining. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called Chase and was informed the card was over its {$21000.00} limit by {$12.00} - the overlimit amount itself was caused by accrued interest charges pushing the balance past the credit line. During this call, I learned for the first time that this card had never carried a 0 % introductory APR. A Chase representative acknowledged that Chase offers other business cards that do carry 0 % introductory APR, confirming that the product line includes the card I intended to apply for. Despite this acknowledgment, Chase offered no remedy. Had I received the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX I intended to apply for, zero interest would have accrued during the 12-month introductory period, and I would have paid the balance in full before any interest began. WHY THIS IS DECEPTIVE : 1. PRODUCT PRESENTATION : Chase markets the XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX with virtually identical visual branding, card design, and page layout. 2. DOCUMENTED INTENT : I possess an internal business financial planning document, authored with my business partner, that specifically identifies the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX as a target card for its 0 % introductory APR. 3. CORROBORATING EVIDENCE : My business partner XXXX XXXX applied for the Chase XXXX XXXX XXXX during the same working session and was approved for it. We were evaluating the same product. NO COUNTEROFFER NOTICE : If Chase determined I did not qualify for the XXXX XXXX XXXX and instead approved me for the XXXX XXXX XXXX, I was never provided a counteroffer notice as required under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act ( ECOA ). I was never informed I was being issued a different product than what I applied for. 5. FAILURE TO MAKE TERMS CONSPICUOUS : The Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) and Regulation Z require that APR terms be clearly and conspicuously disclosed. In a later response, Barclays said it would not assist further, relied on alleged verification calls, and asserted that no new or different information had been provided. Barclays still has not produced the underlying evidence needed to support those conclusions. This is a billing-error dispute under the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z. A billing error includes an unauthorized extension of credit, a failure to properly credit a payment, an accounting error, and a request for documentary clarification. Regulation Z also provides that when a consumer properly disputes a billing error, the consumer need not pay, and the creditor may not try to collect, the portion of any required payment the consumer believes is related to the disputed amount, including related finance or other charges. In addition, in any action to enforce liability for credit-card use, the issuer bears the burden of proving that the use was authorized or that the conditions for liability were satisfied. ( eCFR ) My dispute is specific. I dispute the validity and documentary support for the three payment reversals, the fees and interest that flowed from those reversals and the disputed balance, and Barclays unsupported conclusion that the remaining amount is valid. Barclays has not provided the payment trace data, return codes, timestamps, internal logs, call recordings, transcripts, or agent notes that would be needed to verify its position.

text: Complaint Against Barclays Credit Card Improper Reversal of Unauthorized {$980.00} Charge Dispute I am filing a complaint regarding Barclays handling of a billing dispute involving unauthorized charges from XXXX XXXX XXXX. I initially disputed these charges and the claim was resolved in my favor. However, the decision was later reversed after the merchant asserted that I had previously agreed to recurring billing. This reversal is improper and does not reflect the full facts or applicable consumer protection standards. My account with the merchant had been placed in a paused status prior to the disputed charges. I provided documentation confirming that the account was paused. A paused status reasonably indicates that services and associated billing are suspended. At no time did I receive clear disclosure that charges would continue while the account was paused, nor did I provide express, informed consent for continued billing under those conditions. Additionally, the merchants own process requires a follow-up consultation with a prescriber prior to issuing or refilling medications. No such consultation occurred. Despite this, the merchant charged my account without any interaction, authorization, or fulfillment of their stated service requirements. The merchant has not provided evidence demonstrating that : I agreed to be charged while my account was paused I was clearly informed that billing would continue during a paused status I reauthorized any charges after placing the account on pause Under the Federal Trade Commissions Negative Option Rule and the Restore Online Shoppers Confidence Act ( ROSCA ), recurring charges require clear, informed, and ongoing consent. Prior authorization alone is not sufficient, particularly where account status has changed and no services were rendered. Failure to Disclose Billing Terms During Paused Status The merchants published subscription and cancellation policy does not address or disclose how billing is handled when an account is placed in a paused status. While the policy outlines automatic renewal and cancellation requirements, it is silent on whether charges continue during a paused period. This omission is material. The term pause reasonably conveys that services and associated billing will be temporarily suspended. If the merchants practice is to continue charging while an account is paused, this constitutes a failure to clearly and conspicuously disclose material billing terms. In the absence of such disclosure, no informed consent can be established for charges incurred during a paused period. Barclays failed to properly evaluate whether valid authorization existed at the time of the charges and instead relied solely on the merchants assertion of initial consent. This does not meet the standards for resolving disputes involving recurring billing. These charges were made without valid authorization and without delivery of services, and should be treated as unauthorized. Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

Summary of the dispute : On XX/XX/year>, I was charged {$940.00} by XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX, PA ) for a plumbing service call at my rental property ( XXXX, PA XXXX ). The work performed was described as clearing a blocked sewer main line using a cable snaking machine. I am disputing {$800.00} of this charge on the grounds that the service was not completed as expected. Key evidence of failed service : Only seven ( 7 ) days after the first visit, on XX/XX/year>, the same plumbing company ( XXXX XXXX ) was called back to the same property for the identical sewer blockage problem and charged me an additional {$420.00} ( Invoice # XXXX ). The second technicians own invoice notes confirm that the fresh air inlet the exact access point used on the first visit was still covered, and that the house trap was narrow filled with dirt and mulch. I provided Citi with two invoices from the same merchant one for the disputed charge and a second one, dated just seven days later, for the same work at the same location. I am filing this complaint because my bank, First Financial Bank, denied my fraud claim for several unauthorized XXXX XXXX transactions that were made using my debit card information. Some of the transactions occurred more than 60 days before I discovered the fraud. However, my understanding is that Regulation E only limits reimbursement for losses that occur * * after * * the 60day period. The unauthorized transactions that occurred * * before * * that period are still covered. The bank has refused to reimburse any of the transactions, which does not appear to be consistent with the regulation.

I am requesting the CFPBs assistance to ensure that the bank conducts a proper investigation under Regulation E, restores provisional credit during the investigation, and reimburses the unauthorized transfers. This situation has caused significant financial stress, and I am asking for help in resolving it fairly.

issue: Problem caused by your funds being low
text:
CFPB, I am filing this complaint due to repeated, inconsistent, and unclear information provided by JPMorgan Chase Bank regarding overdraft protection, overdraft practices, and the circumstances under which transactions would be paid, declined, or assessed fees on my checking account. 

Over an extended period of time, I have received conflicting explanations from Chase representatives about whether overdraft protection was available, whether my account was enrolled in any overdraft services, whether transactions would be authorized or declined when insufficient funds were present, and whether overdraft fees could be assessed. These explanations were inconsistent with each other and were not resolved through clear written confirmation. 

At no point was I provided with a clear, consistent, and affirmative explanation of my overdraft status or a meaningful opportunity to make an informed decision regarding overdraft coverage. Instead, I was left with contradictory information that made it impossible to reasonably understand how my account would function in real-world transactions. 

This inconsistency is particularly concerning because overdraft practices involve fees, consumer choice, and regulatory opt-in requirements. When a financial institution provides conflicting or unclear information about fee-triggering services, it undermines a consumers ability to manage their account responsibly and raises serious concerns about unfair or deceptive practices. 

Despite the availability of overdraft options in Chases internal policies, those options were not communicated to me in a clear, uniform, or reliable manner. Different representatives provided different explanations, and no definitive written confirmation of my overdraft enrollment status or opt-in history was offered until I raised concerns myself. 

As a consumer, I should not have to piece together critical account terms from inconsistent verbal explanations. Banks have an obligation to ensure that information regarding overdraft services and fees is accurate, consistent, and non-misleading, especially when those services can result in financial harm. 

The lack of consistent information directly affected my ability to understand : Whether overdraft protection was available or active Whether Chase would authorize or decline transactions when funds were insufficient Whether overdraft fees could be assessed Whether any opt-in or opt-out was on record for my account This confusion is not hypothetical ; it has real financial consequences. A consumer can not meaningfully consent to overdraft practices when the information provided is inconsistent or unclear.

text:
To Whom It May Concern at Kikoff Lending LLC, I am submitting this formal dispute and demand for corrective action regarding the inaccurate reporting of a XXXX past due status on my credit file and the continued reporting of this account despite my prior request to have the account closed. 

I previously notified Kikoff that I requested closure of this account and disputed responsibility for the reported delinquency. Despite this notification, Kikoff has continued reporting a XXXX past due status, which is inaccurate, harmful, and legally improper. This reporting is damaging my credit profile and constitutes furnishing information that is incomplete, misleading, or unverifiable.

Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act ( FCRA ), 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 ( a ) and 1681s-2 ( b ), furnishers of credit information are required to report accurate information and must conduct a reasonable investigation when a consumer disputes reported data. Additionally, 15 U.S.C. 1681e ( b ) requires maximum possible accuracy in consumer reporting. Reporting delinquency after receiving notice of dispute and closure request demonstrates failure to maintain reasonable procedures and failure to conduct a lawful investigation. 

Further, if Kikoff continues to report negative payment history after receiving notice that the account was disputed and requested to be closed, such conduct may constitute furnishing information known or reasonably suspected to be inaccurate, which is prohibited under federal law.

I am demanding the following immediate corrective actions : 1. Removal of the reported XXXX past due status from all consumer reporting agencies. 
2. Immediate closure of the Kikoff account.

3. Permanent deletion of this tradeline from my credit history if Kikoff can not produce competent documentary evidence proving I am contractually and legally responsible for the alleged delinquency.

4. Written confirmation of the actions taken and the results of your investigation.

5. Disclosure of the method of verification used to support any continued reporting. 

Please provide, if you intend to continue reporting, complete documentation including : Signed agreement or authenticated electronic authorization Full payment and billing history Account opening verification records Any communications showing my consent or responsibility Method of verification used during reinvestigation Failure to correct or delete this inaccurate reporting will result in immediate escalation of this matter to the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ( CFPB ), the North Carolina Attorney Generals Consumer Protection Division, the Federal Trade Commission ( FTC ), and any other appropriate regulatory and enforcement agencies. I will also document Kikoffs conduct as potential violations of the Fair Credit Reporting Act and applicable state consumer protection statutes. 

This letter serves as formal notice that I am disputing the accuracy, completeness, and legal validity of this reporting. If you can not provide competent verification, federal law requires deletion of the disputed information. 

Please respond in writing within 30 days of receipt of this correspondence. 

Sincerely, XXXX XXXX

text: I am filing this complaint against Bank of America for failing to protect my account from XXXX XXXX. This merchant engaged in fraudulent practices from day one, forcing me into a contract through deception. I discovered they were stealing money and tried to cancel multiple times, but they refused to stop the unauthorized charges. In a final monitored call on [ XX/XX/year> ] [ XXXX ] with agent [ XXXX XXXX XXXX, I confronted them about the theft. The agent explicitly admitted that XXXX had been stealing money from me. However, they refused to issue a refund, claiming they could only cancel the contract. Bank of America initially provided me with a provisional credit for the total amount stolen since the first day. However, they now plan to withdraw Provisional credit on XX/XX/year>, siding with a merchant that has already admitted to fraud on a recorded line. I demand that the bank request the recording of that specific call and keep the total credit permanent. The bank must not allow a merchant to keep funds they admitted were stolen.This entire situation is a complete lack of respect. I am being victimized twice : first by a merchant that admitted to stealing from me, and now by my own bank for allowing it to happen. I demand justice and the permanent protection of my funds.

I have been with Chime, LLC for XXXX months. 

During that period I have been lied to, hung up on repeatedly by Supervisors in Chime 's employ, hung up on by Member services repeatedly, I have been scolded, told my opinions of service issues are offensive, I have repeatedly requested to file formal complaints and been utterly ignored, asked to be accommodated repeatedly as a XXXX American and been either verbally denied or simply denied by omission and/or disregard of repeated requests, repeatedly told info is sent to my email and when checked there is NO INFO available, Chime, XXXX has refused to contact a scam website and every time I have requested them to contact the suspect website they refuse, Chime then tells me I must wait until XXXX to get my " scammed '' funds back, the rudeness and dismissiveness of the Member Services people is a travesty, and Customer Service IS NOT US based and when I inquire about my concerns, as usual as with most requests for info from Chime, LLC I am denied any reasonable answers, THIS IS THE FIRST TIME IN MORE THAN 20 YEARS OF BEING A XXXX AMERICAN THAT I HAVE REQUESTED AN ACCOMODATION FROM ANYONE ANYWHERE! The response from Chime is literally chilling ... they either deny your request or simply ignore and talk over you, this has gone on for months and nothing changes, I have mentioned that XXXX is the law of the land and NO RESPONSE is Chime 's answer. They do this with impunity and without fear of anyone holding them accountable! There is much more but I am sure I have listed more than enough issues here for you to investigate. Thank You
